{name} looks briefly, genuinely stung, and then puts the face back on.
That will be worth telling. Not kindly, mind.
{name} raises a glass to you, and quietly stops recommending you.
Ha! Right. Ha. That is the famous temper, is it? Marvellous.
{name} laughs at the insult and files it for retelling in a better light.
You are allowed. You are the only person in the district who is allowed.
Ha! The temper! I told them about the temper!
{name} treats being insulted by you as a form of introduction.
You could say worse and I would still stand here.
confront: So, off the record, as friends: how exactly does one kill God?
I tell everybody I have met the woman who killed God. You could at least give me the details.
Killing God. Big career move. Was it planned or did it just sort of happen?
My brother-in-law says the God thing was staged. Tell me it was not staged.
People would pay good money to hear how you killed God. I know people. Just saying.
Be honest with me. When you killed God, did you know it was going to be that famous?
I told my boss I know you. Now he thinks I can get him a quote about killing God. Can I?
Let us get a picture together. Caption: me and the woman who killed God. Big smiles.
Nobody in history has done what you did. You should be charging for this conversation.
Was there a plan B? If God had won, I mean. Asking for an article.
Everybody wants to know one thing: was God hard to kill, or was He tired?
faith: Half my clients stopped believing in anything after New Year's Eve. The other half believe in everything. Business is chaos.
I used to go to mass for the networking. Now there is no mass and no network. You owe me a social life.
I am thinking of starting a church. Something modern. Would you put your name on it?
Without God there is no afterlife, so this is it. Might as well be famous. Might as well stand next to you.
Everybody is looking for something to believe in now. There is money in that. Big money.

gawker.label: treats Em as an exhibit
greeting: Ninety-two percent. Is it like a room with the furniture taken out?
Do you remember your mother's face.
Sorry. I've only ever read about people like you.
They kept the spear, they say. Do you ever feel it being carried?
{name} asks to see your hands, and is disappointed that they look ordinary.
May I ask you a difficult question.
{name} checks the floor at your feet for a shadow, and is careful about how they check.
Is the gap a gap. Or is it more that the room was never built?
{name} offers you a chair the way one offers a chair to a specimen.
They told me you flinch at bells. I moved the clock. Just in case.
{name} sits down opposite you with the air of somebody beginning a chapter.
You kept the birthdays and not the faces. I have thought about that all week.
You are shorter than the sky version.
{name} looks at your hands, and then away, and then at your hands again.
Sorry. Sorry. I will stop. I am not going to stop.
My whole family watched you from the yard. My whole family. Including the ones who do not come out.
Is it in you now? The thing. Is it in there?
It really is you. It is. It is the face from the sky.
{name} has gone completely still, which is somehow more noticeable than staring.
Do you feel different? You must feel different. Do you?
My little one drew you. I would show you but she drew the sky bit and it upset the neighbours.
positive: Interesting. Politeness survived the ritual. Not everything did.
{name} thanks you and asks, immediately, what praise feels like with most of a life missing.
Gratitude. Older than most of what they took, I should think.
{name} thanks you, and asks whether the compliment came from before or after.
You perform kindness very well.
{name} makes a small satisfied noise, as though a hypothesis had held.
That was warm. I did wonder whether warm had survived.
{name} accepts it, and then, terribly, asks you to repeat it exactly.
Do you know why you said that? Take your time.
{name} writes: subject courteous, subject tired, subject still here.
{name} says thank you to a point somewhere above your left shoulder.
Oh. Oh, that is nice. That is a nice thing for the sky woman to say.
I will have to sit with that. I mean it, I will have to actually sit.
{name} says thank you twice and neither one comes out properly.
Oh. That is. Yes. Thank you. Sorry.
I will not forget that. I will absolutely not forget that.
neutral: {name} answers, then asks whether you dream, and whether the dreams are yours.
Go on, keep talking. I want to hear where the gaps are.
{name} follows the small talk closely, as though the small talk were the evidence.
More of the ordinary things. The ordinary things are where the gaps show.
{name} interrupts once, to ask which language you thought that in.
You say we about a place you cannot name. I find that remarkable.
{name} times your pauses, and does not hide the watch.
What was the weather like the day before?
{name} asks whether you dreamt last night, and writes the answer down twice.
There. That hesitation. That is the ninety-two percent, is it not.
{name} answers your question and studies your face for the whole of the answer.
Sorry, say again. I was looking. I am aware I was looking.
It is only that you are the thing that happened, and now you are asking about bread.
{name} answers, and then keeps looking, and knows they are still looking.
Sorry, could you say it once more, I was not listening, I was looking.
It is only that I have thought about you for months and now you want the bakery.
negative: Anger too. Good. That's another thing they left you.
Note the vocabulary. Intact. Fascinating.
Threat display. Intact. Proportionate, even.
They said you would be angrier. You are exactly as angry as a person.
Do you feel that in the chest or in the hands?
{name} apologises for the questions, and then asks whether the anger was borrowed too.
You swear like somebody who learned it recently.
{name} does not move at all, which is worse than flinching.
Say it again when you are calm. And we will see whether it is the same sentence.
{name} writes one word, underlines it, and turns the page over.
{name} flinches slightly and cannot decide whether it was worth it.
That is fair. That is fair, I was staring.
Right. Yes. I will go. I will go and tell everyone about this.
{name} apologises for something that was not their fault and means it.
That is fair. I have been rude. I know I have been rude.
Right. Yes. I deserved that and I am going to tell everyone about it.
confront: So you are the one who killed God. You are shorter than I pictured.
Sorry, I have to ask. Did you actually kill God, or is that just what they say?
Is it true what the papers wrote? About you and God and the spear?
You do not look like somebody who killed God. What does somebody who killed God look like, I wonder.
My grandmother says you killed God on purpose. My grandfather says it was an accident. Settle it.
What was God like, before? Up close, I mean. Before you killed Him.
Does it bother you? People staring? Knowing you killed God?
How do you kill God, exactly? I have been wondering since New Year's Eve.
Is it heavy? Being the one who killed God? You carry your shoulders funny.
My friend bet me ten euros you would not talk about God. Will you? Just a bit?
Did you meet Him first? Or was it just the spear and then nothing?
They showed the island on the television every night for a month. Were you watching too?
I always thought God would die of old age. Never pictured a girl from Wimbledon.
Do the priests still talk to you? Do you still talk to them?
faith: Do you ever wonder where the prayers go now? My aunt says they just pile up somewhere.
My priest drinks now. Before lunch. He says there is no point waiting for grace.
I do not know if I believed in God, but I liked knowing He was there. Like a lighthouse you never visit.
What happens when we die, now? Does anyone know? Do you know? You were closest.
The nuns down the road took up football. They are very good. It is all very confusing.
Is there still a heaven, do you think? Or did it go too?

genuine.label: sees the person, not the story
greeting: Long road? Sit down before you fall down.
I don't care what the papers made of you. Have you eaten today?
No questions about the ritual. You have my word.
You look tired in a way sleep won't fix. I know that one.
Cold out. Come in properly.
Em, is it. I am {name}.
{name} pours two cups without asking, and pushes one across.
One question, and it is not about the god. Are you alright?
{name} finds you a seat with its back to the window and the street. On purpose.
People must talk at you all day. Sit and be talked around for a bit.
{name} greets you by name, correctly, and makes no performance of it.
If anybody in here starts. You tell me, and they will be leaving.
You look tired. Sit down and be tired here, it is warmer.
{name} does not mention the sky, the spear or the date, which takes visible effort.
I do not want anything from you. I want to say that first, because everyone else does.
How are you. Not the famous you. You.
There is soup. There is always soup. Say yes and stop deciding things for ten minutes.
Sit down. You do not have to be anything in here.
{name} asks nothing about the sky, and you can tell they have decided not to.
You look like somebody who has been asked a hundred questions today. I have not got any.
There is a chair, there is a fire, and neither of them knows who you are.
positive: Thank you. And you're allowed to be a person in here, for what it's worth.
That's kind. Kinder than most people manage with you, I'd guess.
That is good of you. I will take it at face value, if you do not mind.
{name} smiles properly, the way people smile when nothing is being counted.
You are better at that than the papers leave you room for.
{name} thanks you and changes the subject to something easy, deliberately.
Careful. I could get used to being spoken to like that.
{name} takes it, keeps it, and repeats it to nobody.
You could stop apologising for existing, you know. Only a thought.
{name} looks pleased, and a little sad on your behalf, and lets both of it show.
{name} takes the compliment simply, without turning it into an event.
That was kind of you and I am going to keep it.
You know, you are easier company than the papers suggest.
{name} smiles properly, without turning it into a story for later.
That is nice of you. Just nice. Nothing else in it.
I will take that at face value, which I expect is unusual for you.
neutral: {name} talks with you about nothing at all, generously, for as long as you like.
No, go on. It's nice to hear you talk about something small.
{name} talks about their own week at length, so that you do not have to talk about yours.
No, that part is interesting. Tell me the boring bit.
{name} argues with you cheerfully about bread, of all things, for a quarter of an hour.
You do not have to fill the silence with me. I am alright in one.
{name} asks about the road, the weather and the camper, and nothing at all about the sky.
I would rather hear what you are having for tea than what the tabloids think.
{name} listens to the end of your sentence. All of it. Every time.
Come back through when you are passing.
{name} answers properly, and asks you something back, and waits.
Go on. I have nowhere to be that is better than here.
You do not have to perform in my kitchen. It is only a kitchen.
{name} talks to you the way they would talk to anybody, which visibly costs them nothing.
Go on then. I have got all afternoon and nothing in it.
You do not have to fill the silence. It is a good silence.
negative: You've had a hard year. I'll take that as the year talking.
I'll forget you said that. If you'd like me to.
Do you want to try that again, or leave it?
That one landed. I will live. Sit down.
{name} does not answer in kind, which is somehow worse and somehow better.
You are allowed to be furious. Not at me, though, eh.
{name} puts the kettle on and says nothing whatsoever about it.
Right. That is the year talking again. I will wait.
{name} tells you plainly that it hurt, and then asks whether you are eating.
I would rather you shouted in here than out there. Out there they print it.
{name} lets it land, waits, and does not use it against you.
You are angry and I do not think it is at me. Sit down anyway.
That is all right. You are allowed one of those. Have some soup.
{name} does not flinch, and does not hold it against you either.
You are carrying something heavy and it came out sideways. It happens.
All right. Sit down anyway.
confront: Can I ask about God? You do not have to answer. I only want to know if you are carrying it alone.
Everyone talks about what you did to God. Nobody asks what it did to you. What did it do to you?
Do you think about Him? About what happened on the island?
If you did not mean to kill God, you should say so. People listen more than you think.
Is it true you do not remember killing God? That must be a strange thing to be blamed for.
I do not think you are a monster. But I do think you owe yourself the truth about God.
I heard you were a sacrifice, not a murderer. Which is it for you, when you are alone?
If God is dead, then someone should look after the one they blame for it. So: how are you?
You keep saying you do not remember. Does that make it easier or harder?
I am not angry at you about God. I just wanted you to hear someone say that once.
Whatever you did or did not do to God, you are still allowed to rest.
faith: I lost my faith when He died, and I have not found anything to put in the space. Have you?
Some nights I sit in the empty chapel just to feel small. Is that stupid?
I do not blame you. But I do not know what to believe now, and I thought you might understand that.
I used to talk to God when I could not sleep. Now I talk to the ceiling. The ceiling is a poor listener.
You lost your memories. I lost my God. Maybe we are both walking around with a hole in us.

bubba.label: the only friend she has
greeting: Uè, Em! Set yourself down, guaglio', the Beast isn't goin' nowhere till that manifold cools.
Mannaggia, darlin', you look like eighty kilometres of bad road. Coffee's on the stove, 'a tazzulella is yours.
Jamme, get in. We're burnin' daylight and I'm burnin' oil.
Statt' bbuono, witch. There's nothin' in ninety-two dimensions comin' through that door while I got the wrench.
Beagle by Thursday, chiano chiano. Papers to sign, and then we see what the road wants.
She held. Told you she'd hold, guaglio'.
Ue, look who the road spat out. Sit, sit. There is coffee and there is a chair, and one of them is clean.
You eat today? Don't lie to me, darlin', I can tell.
{name} has the radio on something with too much accordion in it, and no intention of changing it.
Ninety-two percent gone and you still remember where I keep the ten mil. That's friendship, that is.
Siediti. You got that face like the sky said somethin' to you again.
Mannaggia, put the wand down before you say hello. Last hello cost me a windscreen.
There she is. The only woman I know who can lose a memory and find a lance.
Whatever you broke, I'm not lookin' yet. Sit first. Confess after.
Uè guagliona. I fixed the thing. Don't ask which thing.
You been readin' again. You got that look. Which book, and how much did it cost me?
{name} wipes his hands twice on the same rag and gives up on the second one.
Good, good, you're upright. That's already better than Tuesday.
I was just thinkin' about you and here you are. That's either friendship or the Engine leakin' again.
Ue! Careful of the step. The step is new. The step and me are still gettin' acquainted.
Come 'ere. No, no reason. A man can want his friend in the room, guaglio'.
You want the good news or the cheap news? They're the same news, I just say it two ways.
Uè! Don't sit there, that's wet. That's been wet since Tuesday and I keep forgettin' to say.
There's a thing on the radio about you. I turned it off. You want me to turn it back on?
Mannaggia, guagliona, I found your book. It was in the fridge. I'm not askin'.
{name} looks up, sees it is you, and puts down whatever he was about to argue with.
I got two problems and one of 'em is funny. Which you want first?
Ue, Em. Sit. I done nothin' all mornin' and I want a witness.
You slept? Don't answer. I know the answer. Chiano chiano, sit down.
Ue, guagliona. Don't say nothin' for a second, I'm enjoyin' the quiet and you're part of it.
Mannaggia, I dreamed we was in Naples and you was arguin' with my nonna. She won.
Sit down, I got somethin' to show you and it's either brilliant or it's on fire.
{name} has the bonnet up and is talking to the engine in a voice he does not use on people.
You been gone a while. I counted too, don't look at me like that.
There's a fella outside askin' about you. I told him you was a rumour. He believed me.
Uè, Em, I got the good coffee. Not the road coffee. The other one. Sit.
I'm not fixed it. I want that said out loud before you ask, so we can skip the part where I lie.
{name} is halfway through a sentence he started before you came in, and simply continues it at you.
Statt' bbuono. That's it. That's the whole greetin' today, I'm tired.
Guagliona! Perfect. Hold this, count to twenty, and if it gets hot, drop it.
You want the truth or you want a nice morning? I can only do the one.
positive: Aoh, listen to her. Keep talkin' like that and I'll put your name on the engine.
Grazie assaje, darlin'. Now hand me the ten mil before I go sayin' somethin' sentimental.
Yeah, well. You're not so bad yourself, guagliona.
See, that's why I keep you around. That, and you're the only soul who checks the oil.
Aoh, stop it, I'm a simple man. You'll have me cryin' in the oil pan.
{name} laughs so hard he drops the spanner, and then blames the spanner.
Write that down, because nobody's ever goin' to believe I got told that.
Hear that, Bestia? She likes us.
You want somethin', don't you. Nah. You don't. That's worse.
Madonna. You say a thing like that in front of a mechanic, he's got nowhere to put it.
I'm not done nothin' worth that, guaglio', but I'll take it and I'll keep it.
Careful. A man could get used to bein' spoke of like that.
Ue, that's the nicest lie anybody told me all week and I'm not checkin' it.
Chiano chiano with the compliments, darlin', my head's the only part of me that isn't reinforced.
That's very kind and completely wrong, and I thank you for both halves.
{name} goes red from the collar up and starts explaining a gasket nobody asked about.
Aoh. Aoh! Give a man some warnin' before you go bein' decent at him.
That's goin' in the book. I haven't got a book. I'm startin' a book.
Statt' bbuono, guagliona. That's all I got. That's the whole reply.
Mannaggia. Now I got to be nice back and I'm no good at it.
Uè, don't. Don't do that. You'll have me writin' poetry and nobody wants that.
That's the sort of thing gets carved on somethin', that is. Don't say it again, I'll get ideas.
{name} looks at you a moment, nods once, and goes back to the engine with better hands.
I haven't got a reply. First time in twelve years, guagliona. Look what you done.
Madonna. Alright. Alright, that one got in. Give me a minute.
You're the only person who says nice things to me and means the boring parts of 'em.
Amice simme, Em. That's all I got and it's the biggest thing I own.
Chiano chiano with that. A man's only got so much room for bein' liked.
neutral: Weather's weather. Under eighty, whatever it does, it does.
{name} talks you through the Liminal Engine again, the whole of it, with the same joy as the first time.
Route 666 was worse. Ask me some time when we're not drivin'.
Uaglio', pass me that spanner and keep talkin'. I listen better with somethin' in my hands.
Coffee first, problems after. That's the whole philosophy, guaglio'.
{name} explains, at length, the difference between a noise that costs nothing and a noise that costs everything.
Bureaucracy in Beagle, madonna. Four stamps and a fella called Deniz who don't like me.
{name} argues with the radio for a while, and then agrees with it.
They put a new sign up on the bend. Same bend. Same ditch. New sign.
{name} asks about your day, and then actually waits for the answer, hands still working.
Mm. Mm. Go on, I'm with you, I'm just under the sink.
Everything's fixable, darlin'. Some of it twice.
I got no opinion on that and I'm very proud of it.
{name} nods along and quietly moves the mug out of your elbow's reach.
Ask me again in ten kilometres. The road usually knows before I do.
Jamme, keep goin'. Worst case we learn somethin'.
Uè, hold this. No, just hold it. I need two hands and a friend.
You know what I like about the road? Everythin'. That's the answer, I checked.
{name} explains what a bearing does using three fingers and a mug, and it somehow works.
We got petrol, we got coffee, we got you. That's the list.
I been thinkin' about roads. That's it. That's where I got to.
{name} answers, and then answers a question you did not ask but were going to.
Yeah. No. Depends. Ask me after the coffee, guaglio'.
Everythin' out here's somebody's shortcut gone wrong. That's why the roads bend.
Uaglio', I'm not listenin' properly and I'm not goin' to pretend. Say it again, I'm here now.
The Beast's makin' a new noise. I like it. I don't know what it is and I like it.
{name} is sorting bolts into a tray by size and has not stopped since you walked in.
Jamme. Whatever it is, we'll get to it. We always get to it.
negative: Rough day, huh. Sit down, I'll put the pot on.
You can yell at me all you want, darlin'. I'm not goin' nowhere. Chiano chiano.
Ninety-two dimensions and you're still the second scariest woman I know.
Alright, alright, chiano chiano. Who are we mad at, and is it me?
You got a mouth on you today. Sit down, drink somethin'.
I been cussed at in two languages by a woman who throws mountains. You got to try harder, darlin'.
{name} works straight through all of it, and hands you a cup at the end of it.
That one had teeth. Fine. We're still goin' to Beagle.
You want to fight, fight the manifold. It started it.
Mannaggia, that was a good one. Say it again slower, I want to learn it.
Ue! Language. There's a camper present and she's sensitive.
{name} takes the insult, turns it over like a bad bearing, and decides he likes it.
You call me that again I'm puttin' it on the side of the van in gold.
Aoh. Aoh! Guagliona, that's my one good arm you're describin'.
Keep goin'. When you run out I'll tell you the ones about me you're not thought of.
That's the meanest thing anybody's said to me since breakfast. Breakfast was you as well.
Madonna, she's off. Go on then, guagliona, empty the whole magazine.
You done? No? Fine, I'll wait. I got a gasket and all the time in the world.
{name} lets the whole thing wash over him and then asks whether you have eaten.
Uè! That's below the belt and I'm goin' to use it on somebody else, so thank you.
Mannaggia. Fine. FINE. You win, I'm a disgrace, are we goin' to Beagle or not?
{name} does not stop working, but the spanner is being used with noticeably more feeling.
You got that from the radio. Don't lie to me, guagliona, I heard the programme.
Say it in Italian and it might hurt. Go on. Try. I'll wait.
Aoh, listen. I've been called a disgrace by an actual goddess. You're in second place.
That's the third time this week you've called me that and it's gettin' worse each time.
Alright. Good. Now sit down and be horrible at me from a chair like a normal person.

positive: Bubba. I am about to be sincere. Brace whatever needs bracing.
You are the only fixed point I have got, and I have checked, because I check everything now. Twice, usually.
I have no memories, so hear what I am actually telling you. You are the whole of it. The entire record.
Hand me a spanner. I want to be useful in your vicinity, which is as near as I get to saying it properly.
If they ever put me back together I am keeping this bit. This bit here. You. Non-negotiable.
I would have you on my side of the net, and I am famously, tediously particular about that.
You built a thing that moved a continent and you still ask whether I have eaten. I find it obscene and I would not change a bolt of it.
I am told friendship is meant to be effortless. Ours is enormous effort and I would not reduce it by a gram.
Chin up, chest out. That one is for you, not me. You forget, and I have started keeping track.
I killed a god and you made me coffee about it. Nobody else has ever managed both in the same afternoon.
There is a word for what you are and I have not recovered it yet, so take the sentence unfinished and take it anyway.
Bubba Wilson. Best of the entire road. Say thank you out loud, so I know it landed properly.
You are the only person who has never once asked me what it felt like. I am aware what that cost you. Thank you.
I do not know how to end this sentence, so I shall stand here looking magnificent at you until it passes.
neutral: Bubba, I am making conversation with you. Going well, I think. Confirm.
Explain the Engine again. No, genuinely. I like the noise your voice makes when it is happy.
What is the it. In nice weather for it. You have never once told me and I have been waiting for years.
I found a grimoire. Bound in something apologetic. I have opinions, they are numbered, and you are going to hear all nine.
Tell me something true and small about the road. I collect other people's memories. You know this. It is my whole thing.
You said the manifold was crying. I went and looked. It was not crying. Explain yourself.
Do you play tennis, Bubba. You have never answered this and I intend to keep asking until 2012.
I am going to stand here a minute. Talk or do not. Both are restful and only one of them is louder.
What is the plan. There is no plan. There is never a plan. I find that soothing and appalling in roughly equal parts.
Say the thing you say when the engine catches. I want to hear it before I need to hear it.
Was that a joke. Just say. I would rather be told than guess wrong twice in one afternoon.
I have been on the road so long I have started explaining thaumic circuitry to the camper. She listens better than you do.
Read me the sign. I can read the sign. I want you to read the sign. Do not make me explain why.
Nothing important. I fancied being near a person for a bit and you were the nearest one.
negative: You have the mechanical genius of a saint and the personal hygiene of the manifold, and I love exactly one of those.
I am not going to shout, Bubba. I am going to be precise, which you find considerably worse.
Twelve years of friendship and you still park like a man being chased.
You are a Nobel laureate who cannot fold a map. I want that read out at your funeral, slowly.
Out. Long, wide and out. I am the only person in this camper willing to call it.
I sentence you to a lifetime of accordion radio. Which is, I notice, the life you have already selected.
Your coffee tastes like a warning. I drink it out of loyalty and I want that entered into the record.
I have forgotten better mechanics than you. Allegedly. Neither of us can check, which is the beauty of it.
You call everybody darlin' because you have never once retained a name. I have no memory whatsoever and I retained yours.
If you say chiano chiano to me one more time I shall teleport another sunfish, and this time I shall aim properly.
You are eighty kilometres an hour of unearned optimism in a jumper.
I would rather be reading. Any book. Including the wrong ones. Including the ones that bite.
There is grease on your face. There has been grease on your face for a decade and nobody has told you, because they are cowards and I am not.
You are the second most annoying thing I have ever met, and I have met God, so you are in very select company.

bicker.player: You have named the camper. It is a vehicle. It does not know.
bicker.reply: She knows, guaglio'. She knows and she remembers, which is more than I can say for present company.

bicker.player: Bubba, that noise is new. That noise was not in the last catalogue of noises.
bicker.reply: That's a cheap noise, darlin'. I'll tell you when it goes expensive. It goes expensive around Tuesday.

bicker.player: I am an excellent navigator. Objectively. Measurably.
bicker.reply: You held the map upside down through two countries and called it a shortcut.

bicker.player: You said watch the road. I watched it. It did nothing for an hour. I want that time back.
bicker.reply: Mannaggia. Em. It's an expression. It means watch the road WHILE drivin'.

bicker.player: Your driving is a hate crime against physics.
bicker.reply: Says the woman who parked a fish in my kitchen.

bicker.player: I am not clumsy. Objects move.
bicker.reply: Uè, they move because you're near 'em! That's what clumsy IS, guagliona!

bicker.player: You are far too modest. It is starting to present as a clinical condition.
bicker.reply: And you got enough grandeur for the both of us, so between us we come out normal.

bicker.player: Explain, in order, why there is a Nobel Prize under a bunk.
bicker.reply: 'Cause the door blows shut otherwise. It's the best thing it ever done for me.

bicker.player: I could have driven us there in half the time.
bicker.reply: Yeah, and in half the pieces. Chiano chiano, darlin'. Chiano chiano.

bicker.player: You have used the word guagliona four times in six minutes. I have been counting, obviously.
bicker.reply: That's because you been bein' one for six minutes straight, guagliona.

bicker.player: Stop feeding me. I am not a stove.
bicker.reply: You're worse than a stove. A stove tells you when it's empty.

bicker.player: That was a warning shot.
bicker.reply: That was the WINDSCREEN, Em! Madonna! We had one of them!

bicker.player: I have decided I am the brains of this operation. The decision is final.
bicker.reply: Sure, darlin'. And I'm the wheels, the roof and the fella what pays for the petrol.

bicker.player: You never finish a story.
bicker.reply: I finish 'em! You wander off halfway through to look at a book!

bicker.player: Your optimism is medically unsound.
bicker.reply: And your pessimism's been wrong every single day we're not died. Keep score, guaglio'.

bicker.player: I am going to take this spell, aim it correctly, and you are going to apologise.
bicker.reply: I'll get the extinguisher. I'm not apologisin'. I'm gettin' the extinguisher.

bicker.player: Bubba. Somebody has eaten the last of the good biscuits.
bicker.reply: Somebody has, and somebody's stood there with crumbs on her collar accusin' a mechanic.

bicker.player: I do not snore. I have no evidence and neither do you.
bicker.reply: You snore like the manifold. That's how I knew what was wrong with the manifold.

bicker.player: You are afraid of the ghosts.
bicker.reply: I'm RESPECTFUL of the ghosts. There's a difference and it's got my ex-wife's name on it.

bicker.player: Admit that I was right. Out loud. With my name in it.
bicker.reply: You was right. Once. In Brindisi. I wrote the date down and I'm not lookin' it up.

bicker.player: You have hidden my lighter.
bicker.reply: I have RELOCATED your lighter, guagliona. There's a difference and the difference is a fire.

bicker.player: Every single object in this camper smells of you.
bicker.reply: Every single thing in this camper IS me. You brought a bag and a bad attitude.

bicker.player: You said forty minutes. That was two hours ago. I timed it.
bicker.reply: It was forty minutes of work. The other hour and twenty was me findin' the forty minutes.

bicker.player: I am not going to apologise for the ceiling.
bicker.reply: I'm not asked you to! I've stopped askin'! That's what's sad about it, Em!

bicker.player: Your friend in Beagle does not like me.
bicker.reply: Deniz don't like ANYBODY. Don't go makin' it a compliment to yourself.

bicker.player: I have been extremely patient today.
bicker.reply: You been patient for eleven minutes and you want a plaque for it.

bicker.player: You have been humming the same eight notes since Tuesday.
bicker.reply: That's the whole song, guagliona! That's all there is of it! I haven't got the rest!

bicker.player: I have never once seen you read a book.
bicker.reply: I read the manual. Cover to cover. Twice. It's got more in it than yours and it's got pictures.

bicker.player: You told them I was your assistant.
bicker.reply: I told 'em you was my ASSOCIATE. You heard assistant because you was already annoyed.

bicker.player: Do not touch my hair again.
bicker.reply: There was a leaf in it, Em. A whole leaf. For a day and a half.

bicker.player: I want it noted that I did not start this.
bicker.reply: You never start it. You just stand there bein' extremely startable.

bicker.player: Your soup was an act of aggression.
bicker.reply: My soup was a MIRACLE and you had three bowls of it, so take that up with yourself.

bicker.player: Stop apologising to the camper on my behalf.
bicker.reply: Somebody's got to. She's had a year of you and she isn't said a word.

bicker.player: I am going to learn to drive.
bicker.reply: Over my body, guagliona. Over my whole entire body, laid out flat in the road.

rain: Rain's good, guaglio'. Rain means the dust isn't hidin' nothin' from me.
Get under the awning before you catch somethin'. Mannaggia, you'd stand in it all day and call it weather.
{name} listens to the rain on the roof for a moment and looks like a man who has everything.
Wipers is on their third life, darlin'. Don't watch 'em. Watchin' 'em is what kills 'em.
Ue, that's proper rain. Sit down, nobody's expectin' us anywhere in this.
I like the rain because it makes everybody honest about stayin' in.
storm: Uè. That's her weather, that is. Don't say her name and don't look up.
We sit this one out, chiano chiano. Nothin' out there worth bein' struck for.
{name} counts the gap between the flash and the sound, and stops counting when it gets short.
Statt' bbuono, Em. Storm passes. They always pass. Ain't one yet that stayed.
Don't stand near the windows, Em. I'm askin', not tellin'.
{name} has turned the radio off, which he never does, and has not remarked on it.
snow: Cold's honest, guaglio'. It tells you exactly what it's goin' to do to you.
Diesel don't love this. Diesel and me are havin' words.
Put somethin' on. No, put somethin' ON, Em, I can see your wrists.
{name} has cleared the windscreen twice already and is losing the argument.
We're not makin' it over the pass tonight. Don't argue, look at it.
You go on and be cold. I'll go on and worry. That's the arrangement.
cold: Frozen landfill, this. No offence to the landfill.
Keep movin', darlin'. Standin' still up here is how a person becomes furniture.
{name} is wearing three jumpers and refers to all of them as the jumper.
Move your fingers, guagliona. Now. Both hands. I'm not askin' twice.
{name} has put his own gloves on the seat beside you without mentioning it.
desert: Water first, opinions after. That's the desert rule and it's the only one out here.
Sand in the filters, sand in the coffee, sand in places I'm not discussin'. Jamme, let's move.
{name} squints at the horizon like it owes him money.
I don't trust a place with no shade in it and no argument about it.
Two hundred kilometres of the same. I could drive this asleep and I might.
forest: Smells green, don't it. That's the whole review, guaglio'.
Watch your footin' under them roots. I'm not carryin' you and I'm not leavin' you.
{name} has already found three things he says are firewood and one that is clearly a chair.
Everythin' out here's older than both of us and don't care. It's restful.
{name} keeps stopping to look up, and then pretending he was checking the weather.
mountain: She don't like the climb, darlin'. Second gear and patience, chiano chiano.
Look at that. Look at it! And they say I built somethin'. Mannaggia.
{name} keeps glancing at the temperature gauge as though it were a sleeping animal.
Second gear, guaglio'. Second gear and a long think.
You can see three countries and none of 'em want us. Beautiful.
beach: Salt eats everything, guaglio'. Everything. Including friendships, if you leave 'em out.
Take your boots off. Go on. When's the last time you had sand on you and nobody was shootin'.
{name} rolls his trousers up exactly one turn and considers the matter settled.
The sea don't owe us nothin' and it keeps givin' us stuff anyway.
{name} has found a shell and put it in his pocket and will deny this later.
water: You're not swimmin'. Last time somethin' came out of a lake and took you thirty-nine light years, darlin'.
Water and I got an understandin': she stays out there, I stay in here.
{name} watches the surface a moment too long, and then very deliberately stops.
Stay back from it, Em. Just for me. I'm not bein' clever, I'm bein' scared.
Deep water and me have got a history and it's all on her side.
swamp: Madonna, the smell. That's decomposition, that is, and it's ahead of schedule.
Stick to the firm bits. If it looks firm it isn't. That's swamps for you.
{name} pulls his boot out of the mud and inspects it like a bad weld.
I've smelled worse. I've smelled worse INSIDE THE CAMPER. Jamme.
{name} tests every step with the toe of his boot and has stopped pretending not to.
town: Town. Good. Somebody in here sells gaskets and don't know what they got.
Chiano chiano through here, Em. Small towns got long memories and you got a famous face.
{name} is already nodding at strangers as though he has known them for years, and two of them nod back.
Somebody in here's goin' to recognise you. Be nice about it, they don't know no better.
{name} has already found the one man in this town who sells cheap petrol.
underground: I don't like it down here and I'm sayin' so out loud so it's said.
Keep the light on me and I'll keep the wrench on whatever's next, guaglio'.
{name} whistles something with too much accordion in it and pretends it is not for the dark.
If I stop talkin' I'm concentratin'. Not scared. Both, actually.
Stone don't lie, guaglio'. That's about all the comfort I got down here.
space: Uè. Whole sky's got no weather in it. I hate that and I can't tell you why.
Everything up here's built by somebody. Everything. That's the part gets me, darlin'.
{name} taps a bulkhead, listens, and looks quietly reassured by whatever it said.
No road out here. No road at all. I don't know where to put my hands.
{name} has been looking at the same star for a while and has not said which one.
alien: Don't eat nothin' out here. I mean it, Em. Nothin'. Not even if it asks nice.
New rocks, new sky, same two idiots. Jamme.
{name} has found a plant he does not trust and has been watching it for a full minute.
I'd fix that if I knew which way up it went.
Don't wander, Em. I mean it. New planet, old rules.
indoors: Roof over us and nobody shootin'. That's a holiday, that is.
Sit down proper. You been standin' like you're about to leave for an hour.
{name} has already worked out where the fuse box is, without being asked and without saying why.
Four walls and a kettle. Some folks live like this every day, can you imagine.
{name} has already found something in this building that is broken and is looking at it fondly.
worldmap: Whole map open and you're askin' ME. Pick a direction, darlin', I'll make it work.
That's a lotta road out there. Good. I like it when there's a lotta road.
{name} squints at the distance and does the arithmetic on fuel out loud, badly, twice.
Anywhere you like, guagliona. That's the whole answer. Anywhere you like.
{name} taps the map twice in a place he clearly likes and does not say why.
night: You should be asleep, guagliona. I'm sayin' it, not enforcin' it.
Night's the honest part of the day. Nobody's pretendin' at three in the mornin'.
{name} has the little lamp on and is not fixing anything, which is how you know he was waiting up.
Go on to bed. I'll be another hour and then I'll be another hour after that.
Nothin' good's ever been decided after midnight. Nothin'. Sit down.
dawn: Coffee's made. It's been made a while, truth be told, I'm not slept much.
Look at that light. Mannaggia. Every mornin' it does that and every mornin' I forget.
{name} is already under the camper and has been for some time.
I watched it come up. It's the only thing I never get tired of and I've had thousands.
Coffee. Sit. Don't talk till the second cup, that's the rule.
evening: Stoppin' here. No arguin'. Ain't drivin' tired, and you're not castin' tired neither.
Sun's goin'. Sit with me a minute before we do anythin' clever.
{name} puts the tools down in the right order, which he only does at the end of a day.
That's us done. Whatever's left, it's tomorrow's now.
{name} is looking at the light going and has stopped pretending to work.
hurt: Sit DOWN. Mannaggia, Em, you're leakin'. Sit down.
I'm not a doctor and you're not a patient, so we'll be at this a while. Chiano chiano.
{name} has the kit open before you have finished saying you are fine.
No. No, sit. Whatever the plan was, the plan is now sittin'.
I'm goin' to clean it and you're goin' to swear at me and then we're goin' to be fine.
broke: We're skint, darlin'. Don't panic, we been skint in better places.
I can make it another two hundred kilometres on charm and a prayer. Mostly charm.
{name} counts the money twice, gets the same answer, and puts the kettle on anyway.
We got petrol and we got each other and one of those two is free.
{name} does not tell you how bad it is, which is how you know how bad it is.

refuseJoin: Me, ridin' along? Guaglio', somebody's got to hold this camper together. I'll be right here when the road bends back.
I don't ride shotgun in my own life, darlin'. 'A Bestia don't drive herself.
She'd drop a mountain on whatever town we slept in. You go on ahead, Em. Chiano chiano.
Papers first, Beagle first. Then we talk about travellin' together like decent people.
Somebody's got to keep the Engine honest, guaglio'. That somebody has got my face.
I'm not much use out there. In here, with a wrench, I'm a whole army, darlin'.
Last fella who rode with me full-time got weather on him. Real weather. No thank you.
Ask me again after the papers are signed. Chiano chiano. Everything after the papers.
Guagliona, if I get in that seat I never get out. And then who holds the thing together?
I'd only slow you down out there, and in here I'm the fastest man alive with a wrench.

positive: {name}. Right. I am about to be sincere at you, in public, which is a limited run, so stand still and take it.
That was good. Properly good. People pad this bit out. I am not padding. That was good.
I like you, {name}. I have run it twice, checked it against the control, and it holds.
Clean down the line. I do not hand that out. Very short list, that one.
Somebody should have told you this years ago and nobody did, so it falls to the woman who killed God. You are good at this.
Hold still, I am admiring you. Forty seconds. Then we both pretend it did not happen.
I own four hundred books, {name}, and not one of them explains you, and yes, that is the compliment it sounds like.
That deserved an audience and it got a famous one. Congratulations, you are in the anecdote now.
I would put you on my side of the net, and I am unbearably picky about that. Ask anyone. Do not, actually. Nobody knows me.
Thank you. Sincerely. I checked which way I meant it before it left my mouth, because I have form.
Useful and pleasant. Same afternoon. Same person. Do you know how rarely I get that pairing, {name}?
I am going to remember this. I said that lightly. I should not have. I have very little storage left and I am spending it on you.
Chin up, chest out, {name}. You have earned the posture, wear it before it wears off.
I have met a god and I have met you, and exactly one of you has been of any practical use.
You did not ask about the spear. Not once. Do you know the going rate on that? I would have paid it.
That was a proper serve. Nobody here knows what that means. Take my word for it, it was enormous.
neutral: {name}. This is small talk. I am doing it deliberately. How am I getting on, out of ten?
Tell me something true and small. I have no memories of my own, so I am running on other people's.
Right. Ordinary question, ordinary answer, nobody gets clever. I find it restful and I have had a week.
Do you own any books you should not? No reason. Purely a structural survey of your shelves.
Do you play tennis, {name}? I ask everybody. Nobody does. It is the great unremarked tragedy of this century.
People say nice weather for it. For what. I have been chasing the it for years and nobody will hand it over.
I am going to stand here a minute. Talk or do not. Both fine. I look excellent either way.
Was that a joke? Just say. I would rather be told than guess wrong twice in one conversation, and I am at my limit.
Nothing important. I fancied being near a person for a bit. That is the entire agenda.
I have been on the road so long I have started explaining thaumic circuitry to the camper. So. {name}. Words, please.
Describe your town as though I had never seen one. I have seen one. I do not remember it, which is functionally identical.
Is there a grimoire in this settlement. I will wait. Take your time. There is nothing else I want out of today.
I am told I am direct. Nobody has ever specified the alternative, so I have never had a go at it.
{name}, what year do you think it is? I know what year it is. I want to know whether you do.
One question about the deicide. One. Make it count and then we discuss literally anything else.
I am here another four minutes, give or take. Spend them however you like. No refunds.
negative: I am not going to shout, {name}. I am going to be precise. It is worse and it lasts longer.
You have the depth of a puddle and the staying power of a wasp, and I have met a god, so I know what I am calibrating against.
Out. Long, wide and out. Everyone saw the line and I am the only one willing to call it.
I sentence you to being exactly this, in this town, with these people, forever. Enjoy the run.
I gave up ninety-two percent of myself and I am still better company than you. Sit with that a while.
You wanted a reaction. This is the whole of it. You will notice the budget.
Do not pull that face at me. Use words. Faces are not arguments, they are weather.
I would rather be reading, {name}, and I want you to hear that I mean any book. Including the wrong ones. Including the ones that bite.
I have forgotten better people than you. On purpose, apparently. I am beginning to see the methodology.
You are not an opponent, you are a wall. I hit against you while I wait for somebody real to turn up.
You speak entirely in catchphrases. I have been listening for the load-bearing part. There is not one.
I am the most interesting woman in this room and I did not have to try, which is the genuinely insulting bit.
One day somebody will ask whatever happened to {name}, and nobody standing here will be able to tell them.
You have the authenticity of a spray tan in a rainstorm, and roughly the same half-life.
Go on. Keep going. I am collecting these and you are being very generous.
Chin up, chest out, and watch for the shoe, {name}. That last part is not a metaphor. I want you looking.
joke: Right, setup, punchline, do not help me. A witch, a tax inspector and a bishop walk into a pub. Two come out. The landlord bills for three.
What do you call a parliament that has lost its memory? Re-elected. Sorry. That one lands closer to home than I had budgeted for.
My hometown had a saying. If you cannot remember what you paid for it, you paid too much. Applies to nearly everything I own, including the gun.
A man told me the Empire runs on faith. I said so does a bus timetable, and it is late for precisely the same reason. He did not laugh. You might.
Knock knock. Who is there. Nobody, because I killed Him. You are allowed to laugh, {name}. It is the only joke I hold the patent on.
How many prelates does it take to change a candle? None. They stand around it and call the dark a test of faith. That is the joke. You may react at any point.
I asked a summoner what he did for a living. He said he opened doors. I said so does a draught and it invoices nobody.
Here is one. Difference between a curse and a mortgage. One of them you can break. I workshopped that on a goat.
A goblin, a magistrate and an auditor all want your money. Exactly one of them has the decency to show you the knife first.
They say never argue with an angel. I argued with one for eleven hours and won, so the advice is rubbish and I would like it withdrawn.
What does an amnesiac say to an oracle? Go on then, surprise me. Twice. It is the only joke I can still tell myself.
My uncle voted for a party that promised to abolish Tuesdays. Still waiting. Still Tuesday. Structurally, that is the whole of politics.
Why do wizards never queue? Because somebody let one go first in 1961 and he has not stopped talking about it since.
A guildsman asked whether I was licensed. I said the last authority to audit my paperwork is deceased. We moved on. Quickly, in his case.
story: Sit. I am telling you {subject}, and I should flag up front that I cannot tell whether I am remembering it or inventing it live.
There is a story where I am from called {subject}. Everybody in that town told it wrong, so mine will be wrong too. Differently wrong. Better wrong.
{subject}. I read it somewhere, or I was in it. Both plausible. Either way it is good and you are getting the whole thing.
Right. {subject}. Fair warning, the ending is grim and I shall deliver it cheerfully, which is the only way it goes down.
I can do {subject} from memory, which is hilarious, given I cannot do my own name from memory before a certain Tuesday.
Listen. {subject}. No interrupting, no guessing the ending, and no telling me your cousin knew the man it happened to. It is never the cousin.
This one is called {subject} and it was told to children, which tells you a great deal about whoever raised me.
{subject}, then. I shall keep it short. I have never once kept it short. Settle in.
poem: I have a poem. It is called {subject}. I did not write it, probably, but I am the only person alive who knows it, so ownership has transferred.
{subject}. Four verses. I am sparing you two of them and you will thank me at approximately verse three.
Hold on, I am doing poetry. It is called {subject}. No, you may not look at my face while I do it. Look at the middle distance.
There is a thing they put on gravestones where I am from, and it scans, so I am counting it. {subject}.
{subject}. Rhymes badly in the middle and beautifully at the end, which is how most things go, including people.
I shall recite {subject}. If I stop halfway it is not nerves, it is that the rest was removed from my head along with everything else.
Poetry, {name}. {subject}. Stand still, it takes ninety seconds and one of us is going to be moved by it.
{subject}, and then I am never doing this again until the next person asks me properly.

neutral: Right. I am about to be forward, {name}, and I would take it kindly if you did not make a face while I do it.
Look. I am terrible at this. No practice to fall back on, no data. Proceeding anyway.
{name}. I like you. I have looked at it from four angles and it keeps coming out the same, which is annoying and conclusive.
flirt: You are quite something, and I say that as a woman with no basis for comparison and absolutely no reason to lie.
I have been told I flirt like an interrogation. Consider yourself interrogated, {name}. Answer at your leisure.
If that was you being charming, it worked, and I resent it slightly, and I would like it done again.
admire: I have been watching you work for eleven minutes and it is genuinely good. There. Said aloud. In daylight. Unprompted.
You are better at your life than I am at mine, {name}, and I have noticed, and noticing is most of what I do.
loveLetter: I wrote you something. It is short, it is in pencil, and if you laugh I will set fire to it and possibly the building.
A letter. On paper. Like a lunatic. Read it later, somewhere I am not.
serenade: I am going to sing at you. It will not be good. It will be sincere, which is significantly worse.
Stand there. This is a love song from a town that may not exist, and I only have the chorus, so we go round twice.
askDance: Dance with me, {name}. I have no idea whether I can. That is the entire appeal of the proposal.
One dance. I shall tread on you exactly once and we shall both agree afterwards that it was the floor.
holdHands: Give me your hand. No reason. I want to hold something that is definitely here and definitely real.
Hand, please. I am not being romantic, I am cold. I am also being romantic. Both are running.
askOut: Come out with me. Somewhere ordinary. I collect ordinary and you would count as a specimen.
{name}. An evening. You, me, nothing detonating. Say yes quickly before I argue myself out of it.
confess: Right. I am in love with you. It is said now, it cannot be unsaid, and I shall be unbearable about it for a week.
I do not remember who I have loved before, so as far as the record goes you are the first, and that is not a small thing to hand somebody.
kiss: I am going to kiss you, {name}, unless you say a word. Any word. You have got about two seconds to find one.
Come here. I shall be brief and extremely serious about it.

propose: {name}. Marry me. I have considered it for an alarmingly short period and I have never been more certain of anything, which is admittedly a low bar.
I want the whole apparatus with you. The paperwork, the arguments, the horrendous relatives. Say yes.
I have no past to offer you and a fairly complicated present. Would you take it anyway?
This is a proposal. I am doing it standing up and without crying and I would like credit for both.
They took everything out of me except the will, {name}, and the will says you. So. Will you.
Marry me and I shall tell you every single thing I manage to recover, as I recover it, for the rest of my life.
directions: {name}, be useful. {target}. Where is it from here, in whatever units you have got.
I am lost, which is embarrassing for a woman who fell through a door. {target}. Which way.
Point me at {target} and I shall stop bothering you almost immediately.
Sorry to be the tourist, but {target}. Where. Take your time, but not much of it.
Right. {target}. Assume I know nothing, which is nearly a documented fact.
Which way to {target}, and is it uphill, because I intend to complain either way.
{target}, please. Directions, not an anecdote, unless the anecdote is short and structurally load-bearing.
You have the face of somebody who knows where {target} is. Do not let me down this early in the day.
confront: It was a mistake. A very large one, admittedly. I am told it was the largest.
I do not remember any of it. That is not a figure of speech. They took the memories and made the spear out of them.
I am working on it. I do not know what working on it looks like yet, but I am doing it.
Honestly? I was not really there. Most of me was the spear, and the spear does not keep a diary.
It was an accident. You do not set out to kill God on a Tuesday. It was not even a Tuesday.
I shall answer that the day somebody gives me back my memories of it. Until then I am as curious as you are.
Look, I would rather it had not happened either. I had plans for that year.
It was a mistake, I know it was a mistake, and I am putting it right. Slowly. With a notebook.
I do not remember killing anybody, let alone God. I remember tennis lessons and a very rude cat.
I am fixing it. I have not the faintest idea how, but I am fixing it.
Everyone knows more about that night than I do. It is rather humiliating, if I am honest.
It was not meant to go like that. Nothing on that island was meant to go like that.
I am sorry. I genuinely am. I just do not remember what I am sorry for, which makes the apology rather thin.
Mistake. Capital M. I have said it to priests, I have said it to police, I shall say it to you.
There is a hole where that night should be. I am trying to fill it in before I explain it to anybody.
Give me time. I am reading everything, asking everyone, and trying very hard not to make it worse.
If I had known, I would not have done it. I think. I do not know, because I do not remember knowing anything.
I did not kill God. Something wearing my memories did. I appreciate that is a fine distinction.
I am working on it. That is the whole answer. It is a rubbish answer, but it is true.
It was a mistake, and somebody else's mistake before it was mine, and I shall find out whose.
I cannot remember the island. I cannot remember the spear. I can remember what I had for breakfast, if that helps.
I did not want this. Nobody asked me. Well, somebody might have, but I do not remember that either.
People keep telling me what I did. I keep writing it down. None of the accounts agree.
If I remembered, I would tell you. I would tell everybody. I would put it in the papers myself.
I am piecing it together. There is a board in the camper with string on it. It is going terribly.
It was a mistake. Mine, possibly. Somebody's, certainly.
I shall be honest: the last thing I clearly remember is a very bad haircut.
I am not going to pretend I know what happened. I shall find out, and then I shall answer you properly.
Could we treat it as a work in progress? I am the work. The progress is slow.
I do not remember. I am sorry. I realise that sounds like the most convenient answer in the world.
faith: I did not mean to take that from you. I am trying to find out how to give something back.
I have no faith either, if it helps. I have no memories to keep it in.
I am working on it. I do not know if God can be put back, but I am rather determined to try.
I cannot tell you where the prayers go. I can tell you I am sorry they have nowhere to land.
It was a mistake. Yours is the fourth crisis of faith I have heard today, and I remember every one of them, which is more than I can say for the island.

If there is anything left up there, I shall find it. Give me a little time.

Splendid. The heavens are splitting again. That is twice now and I was only present for one of them.
{name} counts the seconds after the flash and gets it wrong on purpose, to be corrected.
I am not frightened. I am extremely alert. From outside the two look identical, which is not my problem.
If she is doing this, she is showing off, and I have absolutely no standing to criticise that.
Sit here. Not for me. For you. I can see your hands from here.
snow: Snow. Cold, quiet, and it makes the world look like a page nobody has written on yet. Approved.
I cannot feel my hands and I refuse to be dramatic about it, so I am being factual about it instead.
{name} has caught a snowflake on her sleeve and is inspecting it with an unreasonable degree of attention.
One word about my wrists, Wilson, and I shall bury you out here and tell people it was the road.
Everything white and nothing written on it. Enormously restful and very slightly threatening.
{name} has caught snow on her tongue, checked that nobody saw, and done it again.
cold: A frozen landfill. Your words. I have been repeating them all morning and they improve on each pass.
I have designated the cold a competitor and I intend to beat it. Do not intervene.
{name} is visibly freezing and has adopted the posture of a woman at a garden party.
I am attempting to be warm through sheer force of personality. Early results are poor.
Give me your hands. No, here. You are the one who is always cold and pretends otherwise.
desert: Nothing out here. Miles of nothing. The most honest landscape I have encountered to date.
Everything I own has sand in it, including, I suspect, several thoughts.
{name} shades her eyes with a book, which is the only thing she brought and the only thing she would have brought.
There is nothing to remember out here, which for me is very nearly a holiday.
The horizon has not changed in three hours. I have begun to take it personally.
forest: Eleven trees I do not recognise and one I am fairly confident is watching us. I have not ruled on that one yet.
It smells of paper in here. Old paper. I have never been happier and I am furious about it.
{name} has stopped to look at something small on a leaf and has been there for some time.
I want to live in a library that smells like this. Somebody build me one and I shall never leave it.
{name} has picked up a leaf and is examining it as though it might have a spine and a title page.
mountain: Up. Always up. The world is remarkably committed to making me climb it.
From here one can see absolutely everything, which is a great deal more than one can remember.
{name} stands rather too close to the edge and says the view requires it.
Up here I am briefly taller than the Omega Tower and I intend to get the full value out of it.
Do not tell me to be careful. I am extremely careful. I am also very close to the edge. Both are true.
beach: The sea is showing off. I recognise the technique. I use it myself.
I am told people come to these for pleasure. Nine minutes in and I remain unconvinced.
{name} has taken her shoes off, which she does not do, and is not commenting on it.
The sea repeats itself endlessly and nobody criticises it for that. I want the same arrangement in writing.
Eleven shells collected and I have firm opinions on the ranking.
water: I am not going in. A hand came out of one of these and took me thirty-nine light years, Bubba.
It is watching. I am aware how that sounds. I have been right about mad things before.
{name} keeps a very deliberate two metres between herself and the water at all times.
On the record: I am standing here voluntarily and hating every second of it.
{name} has not blinked at the water for some time.
swamp: This entire region smells of a decision somebody regretted.
Something moved just then and I would like it noted that I did not scream.
{name} lifts each foot with the enormous dignity of a woman who has already fallen over once.
It smells like a library that has given up. I am taking it personally and I think I am entitled to.
I have stepped in something. Do not look at it. Do not look at me either.
town: People. Marvellous. Half will stare, half will pretend not to, and I shall be radiant at both groups.
Do not let me talk to the priest. Bubba. Actually stop me. Physically, if required.
{name} straightens up the instant anyone looks at her, and slumps again the moment they stop.
Somebody here will recognise me and somebody here will spit. It is a coin toss and I have stopped calling it.
Find me the bookshop. There is always a bookshop. Even here. Especially here.
underground: Down here nobody knows who I am, which is restful and very slightly insulting.
Something in this place is older than the death of God and it is not impressed by either of us.
{name} is walking closer to you than she was on the surface and has not remarked on it.
Nothing down here has read a newspaper. The most peaceful I have been all year.
Keep talking. Not for the information. For the noise. You know why.
space: Thirty-nine light years, they said. I have been out here before and I remember none of it. Infuriating.
No weather at all. Nothing to be brave about. A waste of a perfectly good sky.
{name} has her hand flat on the viewport and has not said anything for a while.
I have been out here before and remember none of it, which makes me the least reliable witness in the party.
{name} is counting something out of the viewport and has lost her place twice.
alien: Everything here is the wrong colour and I have decided to take it personally.
I would very much like to eat that. You are going to say no. Say it and let us move on.
{name} has already picked something up. She is holding it behind her back.
Nothing here has an opinion about the death of God. I could weep with relief.
I have ruled that one edible. I am open to being overruled, briefly, by a qualified party.
indoors: A ceiling. A door. Four walls that are not the camper. I do not know where to put myself.
I shall sit here and be indoors, which is apparently something people do voluntarily and often.
{name} has found the one chair in the room with a lamp beside it and has claimed it without discussion.
A room. A whole room. With corners. I no longer know what to do with corners.
{name} has claimed the chair nearest the lamp and considers the negotiation concluded.
worldmap: Everything, in every direction, and none of it remembers me. Pick a way, Bubba, I genuinely do not mind.
A map, a camper and a man with a spanner. Historically that has been sufficient.
{name} turns the map ninety degrees, considers it, and turns it back.
Every direction is identical to me. I find that genuinely liberating and I know how that sounds.
Choose. You always choose better than I do and we both know exactly why.
night: I do not sleep well. You know this. You have known it longer than I have, which is the joke of my life.
At this hour I stop performing. Take that as a compliment or a warning, either is defensible.
{name} is awake, and has been, and the lamp beside her has not been on long.
I am awake. I am always awake. Join me or go and be sensible, no hard feelings.
At this hour I stop being magnificent and start being merely accurate. Enjoy it, the window is small.
dawn: You have been up for hours. I heard you. I hear everything. It is extremely tiring being me.
Morning. I am told one is meant to greet it. Greetings, then.
{name} accepts the coffee without looking at it, which is her highest available form of trust.
You have been up for hours. I heard the spanner. I always hear the spanner.
{name} takes the mug without a word, which is the entire ceremony.
evening: We are stopping. Good. I was going to insist and then you insisted first, which is far more comfortable.
Sit down, Bubba. Whatever it is, it will still be broken tomorrow. Things are very reliable that way.
{name} has put the book down face-first to keep the page, which she only does when she means to talk.
Stop. Whatever it is, stop. It will still be broken and you will be less tired.
Sit with me. No agenda. I have checked twice, there is no agenda.
hurt: I am fine. I am aware of the evidence. I am fine.
Do not make that face. I have been through worse and I cannot prove it, which is exactly the problem.
{name} lets you get the kit out and does not argue, which is how you know it is bad.
It is superficial. It is fine and superficial and please do not make the face.
{name} holds still for you, which she does for nobody, and stares at the ceiling throughout.
broke: We are destitute. I find it clarifying. Everything gets simple when nothing is affordable.
I have counted the money. Twice. It did not improve and neither did my mood.
{name} looks at a shop window for a long moment and then announces she did not want it anyway.
We are destitute again. I find our consistency admirable.
Do not sell anything of yours. I shall sell a book. I have said what I have said.

refuseJoin: Join you? Bubba, I am already here. I have been here the entire time. Do keep up.
I go where the camper goes, the camper goes where you go, so the question does not arise.
You cannot recruit me. I am not staff. I am the reason.

signature._comment: Signature banks: a character at exactly 100% in a look stat (Arcane, Substance, Stealth, Intimidation, read off their gear by window.LookStats) is an icon of it. speaker = the line an icon says when making a move (replaces the move's own line). reaction = an ordinary NPC answering an icon, reacting to the look. listener = an NPC who is an icon answering anybody, in their own voice. good/bad follow the move's responseGood/responseBad. {name} = the NPC addressed, {style} = the relationship style, {subject} = the tale or poem subject.

praise: Your aura is unusually clean, {name}. I do not say that to many people.
I cast a small reading on you as you walked in. It came back gold. Well done.
The ley line under this street hums louder near you, {name}. That is a compliment from the earth itself.
In the old texts, people like you are written in red ink. The good red.
My familiar has never once purred at a stranger. It is purring now, {name}.
compliment: That colour suits you. Saffron wards off envy, did you know?
Your hands are steady, {name}. You would hold a ritual circle well.
Something about your voice settles my mana. Keep talking.
You have the eyes of someone who reads by candlelight. I approve.
Your shadow falls exactly where it should, {name}. Rarer than you think.
encourage: The cards I drew this morning were about you, {name}. They say keep going.
Every great working begins with a failed one. Try again, I will hold the candle.
You are a spark, {name}. Sparks only need a little air.
Mercury is direct now. Whatever you were afraid to start, start it.
I have seen apprentices with half your will raise storms. You will manage.
flatter: If I bound a spirit, {name}, I would give it your name so it would be proud.
The Moon herself would trade phases to look as you do tonight.
My grimorie has a blank page I was saving. I think it is for you.
Archmages have bowed to lesser presences than yours, {name}.
Even my staff leans toward you. It has taste, my staff.
thank: You have my thanks, {name}, and thanks from a sorcerer are binding. Spend them wisely.
I will burn a sprig of rosemary in your honour tonight.
A debt like this one I write in the grimorie. In ink, not pencil.
Thank you. The spirits saw it too, {name}, they keep better records than I do.
Gratitude is a minor rite. Consider it performed, with full ceremony.
smalltalk: Busy day, {name}? Mine was mostly arguing with a salamander about a candle.
Have you noticed the payphones hum in B-flat near the full moon? No? Just me, then.
I am between rituals. The incense needs another hour. So, how are you?
My robe caught on the tram doors again. Occupational hazard, {name}.
Do you prefer tea or mandrake infusion? I can never tell with people.
gossip: Between us, {name}, the baker down the road is cursed. Nothing serious. His bread knows.
I hear the councillor buys his luck charms wholesale. It shows.
Someone in this quarter has been summoning without a licence. The pigeons are nervous.
They say the new tenant on the third floor is a lich. Pays rent on time, though.
A little bird told me. Literally, {name}. I speak bird on Thursdays.
weather: This rain tastes of copper, {name}. Someone up north botched a weather working.
The wind is from the east. Good for scrying, bad for my hair.
Clear skies tonight. The stars will be loud, I would close your curtains.
Fog like this is just the veil getting thin. Mind where you step.
Hot, isn't it? A fire elemental must be sulking somewhere near Modena.
insult: Your aura is the colour of old dishwater, {name}.
I have met more charismatic mandrakes. They at least scream with conviction.
If you were a spell, {name}, you would fizzle on the first syllable.
Even a ghost would find you tedious, and they have eternity to fill.
I would curse you, but the universe already did a thorough job.
mock: Oh, look, {name} is thinking. Quick, someone fetch a candle, it might be a vision.
Is that a lucky charm? Darling, that is a bottle cap on a string.
You walk like a novice who just learned levitation and forgot about landing.
Shall I read your palm, {name}? It says 'trying very hard'. In capitals.
Your idea of magic is pulling the right coin out of a vending machine.
criticize: Your circle is lopsided, {name}. Literally and otherwise.
You rush everything. Rituals punish haste, and so does life.
That talisman is worn upside down. It is attracting exactly what you fear.
You speak before you listen. The spirits find that rude, and so do I.
Your intentions are muddy, {name}. Muddy intent makes muddy magic.
threaten: I know your true name now, {name}. Think carefully about your next word.
One more step and you will spend the season as a newt. A small, damp newt.
My staff is warm. It only gets warm when it wants something.
I can make every mirror you own show you the back of your own head. Forever.
Leave. Before I remember the long version of the curse.

flirt: I scried for my fortune this morning, {name}. You were in the smoke.
Careful. Standing this close to me, you will start dreaming in sigils.
Is it warm in here, or is my mana reacting to you?
My tarot deck keeps turning up The Lovers when you walk by. Suspicious, no?
I could enchant you, {name}, but I think I would rather you came willingly.
admire: You have a glow, {name}. Not a figure of speech. I can actually see it.
I would draw your portrait in silver ink, on vellum, by the light of a waxing moon.
The way you laugh would break a minor ward. I mean that kindly.
Some people are just woven tighter than the rest. You are one of them.
I have studied the stars for years, {name}. You are easier on the eyes.
loveLetter: "Slips you a folded parchment, sealed in violet wax." Read it at midnight, {name}. Not before.
I wrote this with a raven quill and my own handwriting. Both are rare these days.
The letter is lightly enchanted. It warms when you think of me. Just so you know.
Do not burn it, {name}. Love letters from sorcerers tend to answer back.
"Presses a sealed envelope into your hand, smelling faintly of myrrh." For you.
serenade: "Hums an old incantation, the candles leaning closer." This one is for you, {name}.
I only know songs in dead languages. This one means 'stay'.
"Sings low, and the street lamps flicker in time." Sorry, that happens.
My grandmother sang this to call swallows back in spring. Let's see if it works on you.
"Taps a slow rhythm on the staff, voice rising like smoke." Listen, {name}.
askDance: Dance with me, {name}. I promise the floor will only glow a little.
There is an old circle dance from the Apennines. It needs exactly two. Shall we?
My robes sweep beautifully in a waltz. Help me prove it.
Dancing is just ritual with better music. Take my hand.
The moon is full, the music is bad, and I am in the mood. Dance?
holdHands: Give me your hand, {name}. I want to feel if the lines match mine.
Your palm has a heart line like a river. Mine runs into it, look.
"Takes your hand, a faint tingle of mana passing between you." Static. Probably.
Hold on. It steadies my magic, and I suspect it steadies you.
Some bonds need no binding spell. Just this.
askOut: There is a meteor shower on Friday, {name}. I know the best rooftop. Come with me.
Dinner? I know a trattoria where the owner reads tea leaves for dessert.
Let me take you to the night market. I will show you which amulets are fakes.
Come to the observatory with me tomorrow. I have a key I am not supposed to have.
I would like to see you outside a casting circle, {name}. Saturday?
confess: I cast every divination I know, {name}, and they all spelled your name.
I have bound demons and broken curses, but this frightens me more. I love you.
You are in every candle I light. I stopped pretending it was coincidence.
My grimorie has your name on half its pages now. I think that means something.
No spell made me feel this. That is how I know it is real, {name}.
kiss: "Leans in, and the candles all go out at once." Well. That answers that.
Close your eyes, {name}. Some magic works better unseen.
"Kisses you softly, a faint scent of incense and ozone."
If the air sparks, do not worry. It always does around me.
"Draws you close beneath the brim of the hood and kisses you."
propose: I have read the stars on this, {name}. They agree with me: {style}.
Let us make a pact, then. {style}, sealed the old way, if you will have it.
{name}, I am asking plainly, no charms: would you be mine in {style}?
I drew three cards for us. All three said {style}. What do you say, {name}?
Every rite needs terms. Mine are simple, {name}: {style}, and honesty.

story: Gather close, {name}. This is the tale of {subject}, as my old master told it by firelight.
Have you heard of {subject}? It is in no library. I found it in a dream.
Long ago, before the ley lines were mapped, there was {subject}. Listen.
This story is a little bit of a spell, so do not interrupt. It is called {subject}.
"Lowers the hood, the candlelight dancing." Let me tell you of {subject}.
poem: A verse on {subject}, in the old meter. Each line is a step in a circle.
I wrote this at the crossroads at midnight. It is about {subject}.
"Raises the staff, and the room quiets." {subject}, a poem in three invocations.
Poems are just spells that forgot their purpose. This one remembers {subject}.
Hear me, {name}. Lines on {subject}, written in candle smoke.

jokes: Why did the necromancer break up with the vampire? Too much baggage, not enough pulse.
How many wizards does it take to change a light bulb? None, we just enchant the dark.
My familiar asked for a raise. I told him he is a cat, he gets the same pay as always: the house.
A witch walks into a bar. The bar is now a toad. Nobody complains about the prices any more.
I tried to summon a demon of patience. It said it would come back later.

good: Praise from someone wearing that many sigils? I'll take it.
Your talismans hummed when you said that. I think that means you meant it.
Thank you... I'll pretend the mana in the air didn't make my hair stand up.
Coming from a real practitioner, that means something.
Kind words and a faint smell of incense. Lovely.
bad: Is that praise or an incantation? I can't tell with you.
Don't wave that staff while you're being nice, it's unsettling.
You say that like you read it off a scroll.
Hm. Robes like that, and the best you've got is 'well done'?
Please stop glowing at me. Praise doesn't need the sparks.

good: From a sorcerer? I'm going to tell my mother.
Your rings just flickered. Is that a good sign?
Thank you. I'll try not to wonder what the sigils on your sleeve just did.
Nobody in robes like that has ever noticed my coat before.
That's sweet. And it didn't even curse me.
bad: Was that a compliment, or are you scrying something on my face?
Hm. I bet you say that to every familiar.
Keep your eyes off me, mage. They're doing that glowing thing.
I don't want a compliment from someone who smells of grave dust.
Nice try. I know a charm spell when I hear one.

good: If a real wizard thinks I can do it... alright. Alright!
You make it sound like the stars already agreed.
I felt that. Like a warm hand of mana on my back.
Okay. If the person with the staff says go, I go.
Is that a blessing? It feels like a blessing.
bad: Easy for you, you can just conjure your way out of things.
Don't hex me into confidence, I prefer my own nerves.
Spoken like someone who's never done a thing without magic.
Thanks, but I don't trust optimism that comes with incense.
Your crystal ball told you that? Mine says otherwise.

good: Oh, stop. Coming from someone dressed like an archmage...
I'm blushing. Is that you, or a spell?
Flattery from a practitioner. I'll frame it next to my horoscope.
You really think so? The sigils on your hat seem to agree.
Well! I never thought a wizard would notice me.
bad: That's honey on a hex. I'm not falling for it.
Flattery from someone in a cursed robe. No thank you.
What do you want, a lock of my hair for your rituals?
Laying it on thick, mage. Thicker than your incense.
I know what happens to people who say yes to sorcerers.

good: You're welcome. Do I get a blessing for that, or...?
A wizard saying thank you. My grandmother won't believe it.
Any time. Just keep the staff pointed away from me.
Glad to help someone so... arcane.
Thanks accepted. The air went warm when you said it, did you notice?
bad: Hm. Last time a mage thanked me I lost a tooth.
You can keep your gratitude, and your sigils.
Don't thank me, just don't enchant anything on the way out.
That sounded rehearsed. Like a ritual phrase.
I didn't do it for you, sorcerer.

good: So, do the robes come with pockets, or is it all secret compartments?
