I've never chatted with a real practitioner. Is the staff heavy?
Nice day. Your talismans keep clicking, is that normal?
Sure, let's talk. Just tell me if I start floating.
Do the police stop you much, dressed like the end of days?
bad: Sorry, I don't talk to people whose shadow moves on its own.
Small talk? You look like you'd rather be summoning something.
Mm. Can you stop humming in Latin while I answer?
I'd rather not. Your eyes keep catching the light wrong.
I've got somewhere to be. Somewhere without sparks.

good: Oh, you'd know all the coven drama, wouldn't you? Spill.
Really? Did your cards tell you that, or a neighbour?
A wizard who gossips! I knew you lot were human under the hoods.
Ooh. Did you scry that? Don't tell me, I don't want to know.
Wait, the baker? I bet you saw it in a bowl of water.
bad: I don't trade secrets with someone who could curse them back to me.
Gossip from a mage? That's how rumours turn into prophecies.
No. Whatever you hear, I bet it ends up in a grimorie.
Keep your whispers. They sound like spells.
I'm not getting on the wrong side of a witch's rumour mill.

good: Is that you doing it? The clouds seem to like you.
Ha, I'd have guessed you could just order the sun around.
Your robes must be warm. Lucky you, in this wind.
Funny, the drizzle stopped the moment you got here.
Right? Even the pigeons are hiding. Or is that your staff?
bad: If you're responsible for this rain, I want my afternoon back.
The weather was fine until you showed up crackling.
Don't talk about the sky like you're planning something.
Can't you just magic it better instead of complaining?
Every time a mage mentions the weather, there's a storm.

good: ...I'd rather not argue with someone who owns a skull candle.
Fine. Fine! Please don't write my name on anything.
That stung. Is that the robes, or did you put something in it?
Alright, I take it back, whatever it was. Just lower the staff.
I'm going. Before my milk turns sour.
bad: Big words for someone dressed as a fortune teller.
Insult me all you like, I've got a horseshoe in my pocket.
Ha! Is that the worst curse you know?
You can't scare me with a dressing gown and glitter, mage.
Did you get that out of an old grimorie? Sounds dusty.

good: Okay, okay. Please stop laughing, your sigils glow when you do.
Ugh. Being laughed at by a sorcerer hits differently.
I'll go, I'll go. Just don't make it permanent.
Fine, I'm ridiculous. You're the one with a moon on your hat.
...Everyone's staring. Partly at me, mostly at your staff.
bad: You're mocking me? You look like a stage magician's nightmare.
Laugh away, wizard. Your hat is bigger than your wit.
Nice one. Did it take a full moon to come up with?
Mock me in Latin next time, maybe it'll land.
You're wearing a bathrobe covered in runes. Sit down.

good: ...You may have a point. People in robes usually do.
Ouch. Fair. Did your tarot say that too?
I'll think about it. Please stop looking through me like that.
Alright, I'll change it. No need to consult the spirits.
I hate that a wizard is right about this.
bad: Criticism from someone who talks to candles? Pass.
I don't need a sorcerer's notes on my life.
Maybe sort out your own aura first.
Says the one whose staff is leaking sparks onto the pavement.
Go read your bones, mage. Leave my choices alone.

good: No! No need for that. I'm sorry, really.
Please, put the staff down. I have a family. And a cat.
...Right. I believe you can. I'm leaving.
The air just went cold. Okay, okay, you win.
Don't hex me, I'll do whatever you want.
bad: Go on then. I've had scarier fortunes from a newspaper column.
Wave your wand all you like, the police here carry iron.
Is that supposed to be scary? You're wearing tassels.
Threaten me with sparks, I'll threaten you with a bucket of water.
Curses don't work on people who don't believe in them.

good: Oh, you're trouble. The kind that comes with candles.
Is that a love charm? Because... it's working.
Flirting with a sorcerer. My mother warned me about this.
Your eyes do this little glow when you smile. I like it.
Careful, mage. I might start believing in magic.
bad: I don't flirt with anyone who has a skull on their belt.
Was that a chat-up line or an invocation?
No love spells, please. I want to choose my own mistakes.
Hm. Your familiar is watching. That's off-putting.
Charming. Literally, I suspect. No.

good: You're admiring me? You're the one dripping with mana.
Oh... nobody in robes has ever looked at me like that.
Stop it. I can feel your gaze, like warm smoke.
That's lovely. Do you see auras? What does mine look like?
Coming from someone so strange and splendid... thank you.
bad: Please stop staring. It feels like you're reading my future.
I don't like being admired by someone with glowing pupils.
Is that admiration, or are you measuring me for a ritual?
Look elsewhere, wizard. Your gaze is making my coins warm.
Mm. I'd rather not end up in your grimorie.

good: Is this... written in silver ink? And it smells of myrrh.
A love letter sealed with a sigil! I'm keeping this forever.
The words moved when I read them. Was that on purpose?
I've never had a letter from a wizard. It's gorgeous.
I'll read it by candlelight. Feels like the right thing to do.
bad: Why is the envelope warm? I'm not opening that.
Half of this is in runes. I can't read it, and I'm scared to.
A letter from a sorcerer. Is it binding if I read it?
It's lovely, but it's sealed in what looks like blood wax.
I burned it. Sorry. It was whispering.

good: That was... the candles leaned toward you while you sang.
Your voice and that hum of mana together... wow.
Was that a song or a spell? I don't care, sing it again.
Goosebumps. Possibly the magic, possibly you.
Nobody's ever sung to me in an old tongue before.
bad: Please stop, the streetlights are flickering.
That sounded like a summoning. Is something coming?
Lovely voice. Terrifying lyrics.
My dog howled the entire time. That can't be good.
I'd prefer a song I can understand, without the chanting.

good: A dance with a sorcerer? Only if your robes don't trip me.
Yes! Do we float? Please tell me we float.
Alright. Lead on, but no levitating me without warning.
I'd love to. Your cloak is going to swirl beautifully.
Is this a ritual dance? Either way, I'm in.
bad: Dance? With all those talismans clanking? No, thank you.
Last time I danced with a witch, I woke up in a field.
I'm not dancing in a circle with someone who carries chalk.
You'll set the floor alight. Maybe another time.
Your staff would take someone's eye out. Pass.

good: Your hand is warm. Tingly warm. Is that normal?
Oh. I can feel the mana in your fingers. That's... nice.
Alright. Just don't read my palm while you're at it.
Holding hands with a mage. My knees have gone strange.
Your rings are cold, but you aren't. I like it.
bad: No, your fingers are sparking. I'd like to keep my eyebrows.
I don't hold hands with people who have sigils inked on their palms.
Sorry, it felt like signing a contract.
Let go, please. My watch just stopped.
Not with all those rings. Who knows what they do.

good: A date? Somewhere with candles, I assume. Yes.
With a real practitioner? I'd be mad to say no.
Yes. Pick me up at seven. {Broom|Tram|Carpet}, I don't mind.
I'd like that. Will you tell me what all the sigils mean?
Alright, but I'm choosing the place. Somewhere without a crypt.
bad: Where would we even go, a graveyard at midnight?
I'm not sure my parents are ready for someone in robes.
Thank you, but no. I don't date anyone who chants.
Sorry, I'd spend the whole evening wondering if I was enchanted.
No. I've read how wizards' dates end, in the evening paper.

good: I think I've felt it too... ever since the air crackled around you.
You mean it? Even with all your mysteries?
I thought you'd cast a spell on me. Maybe you just... did.
Me too. Robes, staff, smoke and all.
I don't understand your magic, but I understand this.
bad: I'm sorry. I can't be with someone who talks to the dead.
That's sweet, but I'd always come second to your grimories.
Are you sure this isn't a potion talking?
I don't feel the same. And please don't try to change that with magic.
I need someone ordinary. You glow in the dark.

good: ...Did the candles all just flare up, or was that me?
That tasted like thunder and honey.
Your lips are warm. Something sparked. In a good way.
Kiss me again. I want to know if the stars do that every time.
I felt that down to my fingertips. Witchcraft, surely.
bad: Whoa, no. My hair is standing straight up.
Not with that skull talisman staring at me.
Sorry. It felt like being struck by a very polite lightning bolt.
I'm not kissing anyone who smells of grave moss.
Please, no. I'm afraid I'd wake up a frog.

accept: {style}, sealed under the moon? Yes, I accept.
If a practitioner says {style} is our path, I'll walk it.
{style}. Write it in your grimorie, then. I'm in.
Yes. Like a pact, but kinder.
I accept. Just promise there's no blood involved.
reject: {style}? That sounds like a pact, and I don't sign pacts.
No. I'm not binding myself to anyone who works with spirits.
I'm sorry. I don't know what your rites would make of me.
That's a ritual vow, and I'm not ready for rituals.
No. Your candles went out when you said it. That's a sign.

good: A story about {subject}, and the lamps dimmed at all the right moments. Bravo.
You tell it like you were there. Were you? In another life?
I swear I saw shapes in the smoke while you talked.
Brilliant. Spooky, but brilliant.
Best ghost story I've ever heard, and I think it was true.
bad: Too many incantations. I lost the plot after the third demon.
A tale of {subject}? I'm afraid that was mostly chanting.
Spooky voice, smoke, candles... and no ending.
I'm not sure I wanted to hear that. My neck is still cold.
That's a grimorie entry, not a story.

good: A poem about {subject}... it sounded like an old spell. Beautiful.
The air hummed on every last word. How do you do that?
Read it again, slower. I think it rhymed in two languages.
That gave me shivers. The good kind.
Like a hymn from a forgotten temple. Lovely.
bad: Was that a poem or a summoning? Because something knocked.
Lots of moons and ravens. Very... robe-ish.
I didn't understand one word about {subject}, and it scared me.
Pretty sounds. Felt like a curse, though.
Poetry from a sorcerer. I'll stick to postcards.

landGood: Ha! A wizard with jokes. The world's full of surprises.
Okay, that got me. Even your familiar laughed.
Ha! I didn't know magic folk could be funny.
Stop, stop, the candles are shaking from my laughing.
That's good! Did they teach you that at the academy?
landGroan: Ugh. That pun should be locked in a grimorie.
Oh no. That's a hex on comedy itself.
Groan. Is that an old druid joke?
I'll laugh, but only so you don't turn me into anything.
That was terrible. I loved it, in a cursed sort of way.
flop: ...Was that a joke, or a riddle from a sphinx?
Your crystal ball should have warned you about that one.
Silence. Even the mana went quiet.
I think that's funny in Old Etruscan, maybe.
...Was that meant to be funny, or prophetic?

good: The sigils hum when someone means it. They are humming now.
Kind words carry weight in the Weave. I will keep these.
Ah. Praise freely given is a minor blessing. I accept it.
My familiar approves of you. That is rarer than my approval.
"touches a talisman" Noted, and bound into the robe. Thank you.
bad: Hollow words leave a residue. I can smell it on you.
The candles did not even flicker. You do not mean it.
Praise from the uninitiated is like rain on wax. It slides off.
Save it for someone who cannot read auras.
My staff stays cold. That tells me everything.

good: You noticed the embroidery? Each thread is a warding glyph.
Few see the robe and not just the costume. You have the eye.
The mana likes being admired. So, admittedly, do I.
This talisman was my teacher's. You honour two of us.
How perceptive. The third sigil is new, consecrated at moonrise.
bad: You called my ritual robe "a nice coat". Leave.
It is not a costume. It is a vow stitched in silver.
Compliment the fabric if you must, but the sigils are not decoration.
My amulet does not need your opinion. It has its own.
Careful. Flattering a focus without permission is bad luck.

good: Hm. The stars said someone would push me today. It is you, then.
Courage is a reagent. You just added a pinch.
Very well. I will finish the circle tonight.
Your words steadied the mana. I felt it settle.
"grips staff" Yes. The working is not beyond me.
bad: Encouragement does not close a summoning circle. Chalk does.
I do not need cheering. I need the moon in the right house.
You speak of effort to one who has fasted three days for a spell?
Spare me. The spirits are more motivating, and more frightening.
Your optimism has no mana in it. I can tell.

good: Greatest adept in Bologna? Well. In the quarter, certainly.
Sweet words, and the incense agrees with you. I will allow them.
You flatter like a minor invocation. Clumsy, but effective.
Go on. The crystal is listening too.
"adjusts the hood" I have been told I channel beautifully, yes.
bad: Flattery is the cheapest charm there is. I deal in better.
I have bound lesser demons who lied with more grace.
Your aura turned grey on the second sentence.
Sweet words are how fae steal names. Mine stays with me.
The pendulum swung toward "liar". Sorry.

good: Gratitude closes the circle. Balance is restored.
Thanks received. The debt between us is unwoven.
Go with the Weave. That was well said.
The spirits heard that too. They will remember you kindly.
"bows over the staff" Gratitude is a ward. Keep it close.
bad: Thanks are not payment. The ritual cost me a year of my life.
Your thanks are vague. Spells are precise. So should you be.
Don't thank me. Thank the moon, she did most of the work.
Mumbled thanks break nothing and bind nothing.
I did not do it for you. I did it for the balance.

good: Mercury is behaving this week. Small mercies, so to speak.
I bought chalk and candles today. Riveting, I know.
The tram hums in the key of F. Did you ever notice?
Pleasant enough. My familiar ate a moth. A good omen.
My TV picks up spirits after midnight. Better than the late film.
bad: Idle talk scatters focus. I was mid-incantation.
I do not do chatter. I do invocations.
You speak, and all I hear is noise over the ley lines.
Small talk. How very mundane of you.
The candle burned down while you spoke of nothing.

good: Oh, I heard too. The tarot told me before the neighbours did.
Cursed, you say? I could have told them. That ring looked wrong.
Delicious. Someone's wards are failing, then.
I scried the same thing in a bowl of ink last Tuesday.
The spirits gossip worse than the market. Go on.
bad: Words carry. Ill words carry hexes. Mind your tongue.
I don't trade rumours. Rumours become curses with enough mouths.
That is not gossip. That is someone's true name. Stop.
The crystal already showed me. You have it wrong.
Gossip is low magic. Beneath us both.

good: Yes, the wind tastes of iron. A storm with intent.
Fine weather for drying herbs and charging talismans.
The rain is cleansing. I left my crystals on the sill.
Fog like this thins the veil. Lovely night for it.
"sniffs the air" Thunder by evening. The sylphs are restless.
bad: Weather is just the elementals arguing. It bores me.
Do not curse the rain. Someone may have summoned it.
The weather is my business. Literally. I did that.
Clouds are clouds. Unless they move against the wind.
I care for the moon, not the forecast.

good: ...That one cut through the wards. I did not expect it.
My amulet cracked. Was that you? It was you.
Rude. The candles all went out at once.
"pulls the hood lower" You have a sharp tongue for a mundane.
Hm. Even sigils cannot stop a word aimed true.
bad: Insult a mage again and you may wake as a newt.
I have been cursed by things older than this city. You are a draught.
Words are spells. Yours fizzled.
Call me a charlatan once more and watch your milk curdle.
Your insults bounce off the robe. It is warded for worse.

good: Laugh at the robe, then. ...It is a little long, I admit.
Oh. That stung more than a failed scrying.
My familiar laughed. Traitor.
You mock the craft and somehow I feel it in my teeth.
"flushes under the hood" The pointy hat is traditional.
bad: Mock the old ways while they still protect you, then.
Laugh. The spirits are laughing too, but not with you.
I have heard better mockery from a poltergeist.
Grin all you like. I know your star sign. I know your weaknesses.
Funny. Remember that when the hexes come calling.

good: ...Perhaps the circle was drawn too small. Fine.
Your critique holds. The third glyph is crooked.
Mm. My master said the same. I hated it then too.
I suppose the incense is a little much. A little.
"looks at the staff" Yes. It needs re-consecrating.
bad: You critique a craft you cannot even perceive.
Bring me your own spellwork, then we will talk.
My method is older than your family. Sit down.
The mana flows exactly as I intend. You simply cannot see it.
Opinions of the unawakened are noted and burned.

good: ...Alright. No need to bring iron into this.
Steel I can ward. Whatever is in your eyes, I cannot.
Very well. I will put the staff down.
"murmurs a protective verse" Let us not test either of us.
Even the spirits are telling me to back away.
bad: Threaten me and I will know your name by sunset. Your true one.
I have stared into the abyss. You are a puddle.
Raise a hand and the ward will raise you off the floor.
Go on. My last attacker still has the rash.
Strange. The cards said you would try this. And regret it.

good: Is that so? The tarot did mention a stranger.
Careful. Flirting with a witch has consequences. Pleasant ones, maybe.
My aura just went pink. How embarrassing.
You're trouble. The good kind, the cards say.
"hides a smile behind the sleeve" Your stars and mine get along.
bad: Charm spells work better than that, and I would know.
My familiar hissed. I trust my familiar.
The pendulum says no. Firmly.
Flirt with the Weave if you like. Not with me.
Mercury is retrograde. Try again never.

good: You look at me as if I were glowing. I suppose I am, a little.
Admire away. The silver thread catches candlelight well.
Few look past the hood. I like that you did.
The mana warms when you look. It is not only the mana.
"lowers the staff a little" That is a kind way to stare.
bad: Staring at a practitioner is how curses start.
You admire the robe. The robe is not available.
Gaze longer and you may see something staring back.
My wards register you as a minor nuisance.
Admiration without understanding. Like loving a book you cannot read.

good: You wrote it in ink, not biro. You understand ritual.
I will keep this between the pages of my grimorie.
It smells of lavender. Did you know lavender binds?
A letter is a spell on paper. This one worked.
"reads it twice by candle" ...I will answer by moonlight.
bad: Paper words, no intent. It will make good kindling for a ritual.
You misspelled my sigil. Unforgivable.
Letters can carry hexes. I burned it to be safe.
Typed? On a word processor? Where is the soul?
The ink was dead the moment you wrote it.

good: The crystals resonated. You sing in a sacred key.
That melody could open a door between worlds. Or just mine.
The spirits went quiet to listen. So did I.
"closes eyes" Sing it again. The candles are swaying.
Music is the oldest magic. You know some of it.
bad: That note banished three minor spirits. And my patience.
Off key. The wards flinched.
Music like that summons only the neighbours.
Even the banshee down the road sings better.
Please stop. The tuning fork on my altar is crying.

good: A dance is a circle, and circles are my specialty.
Very well. Mind the robe, it has warding in the hem.
Lead, then. I will follow the ley lines under the floor.
"sets the staff aside" The moon is full. It would be rude to refuse.
Dancing raises energy. Let us raise some.
bad: I only dance in circles of salt, at midnight, alone.
My feet are bound to ritual steps. Yours are not.
The music is profane. I would lose my focus.
Dancing with you would disturb the charge in my talismans.
No. Last time I danced, something else joined in.

good: Your hand is warm. The mana is flowing between us. Odd.
Hold on. My rings may tingle, that is normal.
Palms touching. You know what that means in palmistry?
"laces fingers" Our life lines cross. I checked.
Mm. Your energy is calmer than I expected.
bad: Do not touch the hand that holds the staff.
My rings are charged. You will regret it. Ah, you regret it.
Your palm says no. So do I.
Contact breaks the ward. Hands to yourself.
I read your hand once already. I did not like the ending.

good: Yes. The next full moon, at the old chapel. Bring candles.
A date. Very well. I will consult the stars, but yes.
The I Ching said yes before you finished asking.
Somewhere quiet. With good energy. And decent wine.
"marks the calendar with a rune" Thursday. Jupiter's day.
bad: My evenings belong to rituals. All of them.
The omens are against it. Three crows this morning.
I do not date. I commune.
Not during an eclipse year. Sorry.
Ask the spirits. They also said no.

good: I knew. The cards have shown your face for weeks.
Say it again. I want it bound into the air.
My heart has its own sigil. You just traced it.
"the candles flare" ...Yes. The Weave says yes, and so do I.
I have read many grimories. None held words like that.
bad: Feelings are a powerful reagent. Too volatile for me.
The stars do not align for us. I looked. Twice.
I am married to the Art. It is a jealous spouse.
That is a love charm talking, not you. Who hexed you?
I am sorry. My heart was given to the Weave long ago.

good: Ah. A seal more binding than any rune.
The mana sparked. Did you feel that too?
"breathes" My wards came down. I let them.
That was a spell. You have no idea which one.
Every candle in the room just lit itself.
bad: Never kiss a mage unwarned. You could catch a curse.
The ward caught you. You will tingle for an hour.
No. Lips carry true names. Mine is not yours to take.
My familiar bit you. Fairly.
That would break a vow I made under a red moon.

accept: Then let it be sworn under the moon. I accept.
Bound. Draw the circle, and we will step in together.
The cards have already blessed it. So do I.
"lights a candle" Yes. Let the Weave witness it.
Agreed. I will inscribe it in my grimorie tonight.
reject: That arrangement breaks the balance. I cannot.
No. My oath to the Art comes first, and it is exclusive.
The augury was clear. Not this, not with me.
I would sooner bind a demon than that contract.
The stars refuse. I am obliged to follow them.

good: A tale of {subject}. There is real lore under that, I could feel it.
You told it like an incantation. The candles leaned in.
Stories are spells with longer verses. That one cast.
I will write {subject} into my grimorie. It deserves preserving.
"eyes glittering" The spirits stayed for the ending.
bad: {subject}? The true version has a curse in chapter three.
You got the ritual wrong. Nobody uses rowan for that.
A story without mystery is just a recipe.
Mundane. Not a single omen in it.
My familiar fell asleep. So did the mana.

good: A poem about {subject}... verse is the first spell. Beautiful.
The metre was perfect. It hummed like a chant.
I felt the veil thin on the last line.
"traces a sigil in the air" I am binding those words to memory.
That rhyme could power a minor ward. Truly.
bad: The metre limps. A spell like that would backfire.
{subject} deserves runes, not doggerel.
Not a drop of mana in those lines.
Rhymes with "moon" and "soon". Every hedge witch does that.
The ancients would have banished you for that couplet.

landGood: Ha! The candles laughed too, did you see?
Okay, that got me. I nearly dropped my staff.
I shall tell that one at the next coven meeting.
"snorts into the sleeve" Even the spirits are giggling.
Good. Laughter clears stagnant energy. Consider the room cleansed.
landGroan: That pun should be sealed in a lead box.
Oh, by the Seven Circles. That was awful. Again.
My familiar left the room. But I am smiling.
Groan. That joke is older than my grimorie, and I love it.
"rubs temples" That one needs exorcising. Fondly.
flop: ...The silence was so total I heard the ley lines.
Was that a joke or a failed incantation?
Even the poltergeist did not laugh.
The crystal dimmed. I think it was embarrassed for you.
No mana in that one at all.

praise: {name}, you have taste. I don't say that to people who buy their coats off a rack.
Well done. Truly. I'd have it framed, if the frame were good enough.
That was first quality work, {name}. Hand-finished, as it were.
My tailor would weep at a seam that straight. Bravo.
Rare to see excellence outside a showroom. You'll do very well, {name}.
compliment: That colour suits you, {name}. Most people wear their clothes. You carry yours.
Is that real wool? Don't tell me. I prefer to believe it.
You have the cheekbones of someone who should be photographed for Maison Varzani.
Lovely posture, {name}. It's half of elegance, and it costs nothing.
Your shoes are clean. You'd be amazed how few people in Bologna manage that.
encourage: Chin up, {name}. Confidence is the one accessory you can't buy, so wear it.
Every fortune starts small. Mine started with a very good haircut.
Go on. Walk in there like you own the building. Half the time, someone does.
Failure is just a draft, {name}. The final cut is what they remember.
You'll get there. And when you do, I'll send you to my tailor.
flatter: {name}, darling, you outshine half the people at last season's gala.
If you were a fabric, you'd be the silk they keep behind the counter.
I've met barons with less presence than you. Shorter barons, too.
You could make a rental suit look bespoke, {name}. That is a gift.
Truly, you belong in a box at the opera, not down here among us.
thank: Thank you, {name}. Put it on my account. Oh, you meant gratitude. Of course.
Most kind. I'll have a card sent round. Embossed, naturally.
I owe you one, {name}. And I always settle my debts, with interest.
How gracious. You've done me a favour worth more than these cufflinks.
Thank you. Manners are the cheapest luxury, and you have them in abundance.
smalltalk: Have you tried the new place on Via Farini? Overpriced, which means it's worth it.
I was just at the cutter's for a fitting. Four hours, {name}. Four.
Do you summer anywhere, {name}? I find the lakes so much quieter than the coast.
My driver took the long way again. I suspect he likes being seen in the car.
One simply cannot get decent linen this time of year. Isn't it tiresome?
gossip: Did you hear? The Contessa wore last year's coat to the auction. In public.
They say the new bank director bought his title. You can tell from his shoes.
Between us, {name}, a certain wizard's robes are dyed polyester. I've touched them.
Old Castelbruni lost a villa at cards. The furniture went before the frescoes did.
I hear the mayor's wife has a dressmaker in Milan she doesn't tell him about.
weather: This rain is murder on suede. I'll have to send these off to be restored.
Glorious sun. Perfect for the terrace and a white linen jacket, {name}.
Fog again. At least it hides the people who dress badly.
Cold enough for cashmere, finally. I've been waiting since August.
Wind like this ruins a good hat. I've lost two this month, {name}.
insult: {name}, did you get dressed in the dark, or did someone do it to you?
That jacket has seen more owners than a used car.
Charming. Do they sell that look by the kilo?
I've seen better tailoring on a scarecrow, {name}. He at least had structure.
You smell faintly of discount, {name}. It lingers.
mock: Oh, how brave, wearing brown with black. Avant-garde, really.
'Is this real leather?' No, {name}. No, it isn't. Bless you.
Look at you, all polished up for the market. Adorable.
Is that a designer piece? Which designer, the one at the bus station?
Don't worry, {name}. Some people are simply born to admire from outside the window.
criticize: The idea is fine, {name}. The execution is off the rack.
You cut corners. I can see it the way I see a cheap hem.
Quality is in the details, and you skipped all of them.
If you want to be taken seriously, {name}, stop dressing like an apology.
That plan has no lining. The first cold wind will go straight through it.
threaten: {name}, I can buy the building you live in by Tuesday. Think about that.
I have lawyers whose suits cost more than your year. Shall I call one?
Do cross me. I could use a new hobby, and you'd make a lovely little ruin.
One phone call, {name}, and no shop in this city will sell you a pair of socks.
Careful. I don't get blood on this jacket. I pay people for that.

flirt: {name}, you'd look exquisite across a candlelit table. Mine, preferably.
I collect beautiful things. Don't be alarmed, I'm only looking.
You've caught my eye, and my eye is very expensive to catch.
Tell me, {name}, do you prefer champagne or something rarer?
Such fine features. I'd have them sketched by a Paris atelier.
admire: {name}, you have the kind of grace that money keeps trying to imitate.
I've stood before paintings worth millions and felt less than this.
Even in that coat, you're elegant. Imagine you in Varzani.
You move like silk on a mannequin, {name}. Effortless.
I don't admire easily. My standards cost me a fortune. You pass them.
loveLetter: 'Hand-pressed paper, sealed in gold wax. Inside: {name}, dine with me.'
I had this written on cotton stock from Florence. The words, I did myself.
'It smells of good cologne. The handwriting is immaculate.' Read it later, {name}.
A letter, {name}. The envelope alone cost more than most love stories.
'A card, thick as a coin, embossed with one line: you are worth the expense.'
serenade: I've hired a string quartet, {name}. They're waiting by the fountain. Shall I nod?
'Hums a waltz from the opera, flawlessly, in a voice trained by money.'
This aria cost me six years of lessons in Vienna. It was always meant for you.
{name}, listen. The cello is real, the bow is horsehair, the feeling is mine.
'Sings low and smooth, like a crooner in a velvet-lined lounge.'
askDance: {name}, may I? I promise I lead better than I tip, and I tip lavishly.
Dance with me. I had lessons as a child. It would be a shame to waste them.
One waltz, {name}. These shoes were made for exactly this floor.
Shall we? The band is mine for the evening anyway.
Take my arm, {name}. Let's give the room something worth gossiping about.
holdHands: Your hand, {name}. Mind the ring, it's older than the republic.
'Offers a gloved hand, kid leather, soft as a promise.'
Let me hold your hand. It suits mine better than any watch.
{name}, you have lovely hands. They'd be wasted on anyone else.
'Takes your hand like it's something rare at auction, and won't let go of the bid.'
askOut: Dinner, {name}. Friday. I'll have the car sent at eight.
There's a table at the top of the Asinelli tower that nobody can book. I can.
Come to the opera with me. Private box, a little champagne, terrible plot.
{name}, I'd like to take you somewhere with tablecloths. Real ones.
Let me fly you to Lake Como for lunch. We'll be back before anyone misses you.
confess: {name}, I've bought nearly everything I ever wanted. Except this. I can't buy this.
All the silk in Milan, and the only thing I think of is you.
I'd trade the villa, the car, the whole wardrobe. Well, most of the wardrobe. For you.
I'm in love with you, {name}. It's the first thing I've had that came without a price tag.
You make all my fine things look ordinary. I can't stand it, and I can't stop.
kiss: 'Leans in, a breath of expensive cologne, and kisses you softly.'
Hold still, {name}. Some things are best done properly.
'Lifts your chin with one gloved finger and kisses you like a closing deal.'
Allow me. I don't rush anything that's worth having.
'A kiss, unhurried and perfectly composed, like a final fitting.'
propose: {name}, I'd like to propose {style}. I'll have the terms drawn up beautifully.
Let's be civilised about this, {name}. {style}. Shall we toast to it?
I've thought it over with my advisor. Just kidding. {style}, {name}. What do you say?
{style}, {name}. I want something exclusive in its own way, like a good label.
Consider this my offer, {name}: {style}. I never make an offer I don't mean.

story: Let me tell you of {subject}. I first heard it at a dinner in a palazzo, over truffles.
{subject}: a story of fortunes won and lost. Mostly lost, by people with bad taste.
My grandfather told me {subject} by the fire in our winter house. Settle in.
Here is {subject}, the way they tell it at the yacht club, which is to say, better.
You'll adore {subject}. It has a heiress, a scandal and a coat worth killing for.
poem: A poem on {subject}, composed in a gilded salon. 'Silk remembers what the hand forgets...'
'{subject}, in velvet dusk and pearl, the city kneels, the candles curl.'
I recited this on {subject} at the Florence gala. They applauded for a full minute.
On {subject}: 'Gold thread, gold light, and you, worth more than both tonight.'
Something short on {subject}. Good poems, like good tailoring, never waste fabric.

jokes: Why did the count fire his tailor? Too many loose ends. And frankly, the man wore sandals.
I told my banker I wanted to feel rich. He said, 'You are.' I said, 'Then stop calling.'
How many aristocrats does it take to change a bulb? None. We have people for that.
My accountant says I spend like there's no tomorrow. I told him tomorrow has a dress code.
A poor man asked me for the time. I said, 'Which watch?'

good: Praise from someone dressed like that? I'll have it framed.
Coming from a suit that costs more than my flat... thank you.
You noticed me? In that jacket, I assumed you only noticed mirrors.
Well. I feel richer just standing next to you.
If someone in silk says it, it must be true.
bad: Easy to be generous when your cufflinks could pay my rent.
Nice words. Nicer coat. I trust the coat more.
Save it for the boardroom.
Praise is cheap. Your tailor clearly isn't.
I don't need a pat on the head from a walking fashion house.

good: From someone in a suit like that? I'll take it.
You have taste, so that actually means something.
I'm blushing. Partly you, partly that tie.
Thank you. I'd return it, but your jacket has heard every compliment going.
A compliment from the best-dressed person in Bologna. Noted.
bad: Slumming it today, are we?
That's what people in hand-stitched lapels say to the help.
Don't praise my shoes while yours shine like that.
Hm. Sounds rehearsed. Like the pocket square.
Keep your compliments, they clash with your cologne.

good: If someone who dresses like money believes in me... alright.
You look like you've never failed at anything. Fine, I'll try.
That's the voice of somebody with a tailor on retainer. Convincing.
Thanks. Maybe one day I'll afford a jacket like yours.
Huh. A pep talk in cashmere. Works better than I expected.
bad: Easy to say keep going in shoes that cost two months' wages.
A motivational speech from the silk department. No thanks.
You've never had to try, have you? It's stitched all over you.
Encouragement's free. You'd know, you've bought everything else.
Go and encourage your stockbroker.

good: Oh, stop. No, don't stop. You're far too well dressed to lie.
If a person with that wardrobe says so, it must be fact.
I could get used to flattery in such fine wool.
Me? Stylish? Coming from you that's practically a title.
You're making me feel underdressed and wonderful at once.
bad: Flattery from the rich always comes with a bill attached.
What do you want? People in suits like that always want something.
Smooth. Like your silk lining. I'm not buying.
I've seen salesmen in cheaper jackets try that one.
Put the charm back in your breast pocket.

good: Thanked by someone with gold cufflinks. My mother won't believe it.
Oh, it was nothing. Really. Is that real silk?
You're welcome. Do people like you usually say thank you?
A thank you that well tailored, I'll remember it.
My pleasure. Truly. You make gratitude look expensive.
bad: A thank you? Frankly, I was hoping for a tip.
Thanks don't pay bills. Your wallet might.
Said like a duke thanking a doorman.
Gratitude from the top floor. Watch it trickle down.
You thank everyone like that, or only the staff?

good: Of course I'll chat. People will think I have important friends.
Go on, I'll talk about anything if I can keep staring at that fabric.
Small talk with a big wallet. My day's looking up.
Is that from one of those Milan houses? Sorry, you were saying?
Funny, I thought people in suits like yours only talked about money.
bad: Shouldn't you be at a gala somewhere?
I've nothing to say to a walking catalogue.
Mm. Sorry, I can't focus. Your shoes are louder than you are.
Small talk? From you? Everything about you is large and expensive.
We've nothing in common. Your buttons are worth more than my week.

good: Ooh, gossip from high society? Tell me everything.
You must hear things at those parties. Lean in.
A rumour from someone that well dressed carries weight.
Who told you? Someone with a yacht, I bet.
Scandal and silk. My two favourite things.
bad: Rich people's drama. Can't say I care.
I don't trade whispers with people who own the street.
Keep your champagne rumours to yourself.
Gossip's beneath a coat like that, surely.
I'd rather not end up in your circle's dinner stories, thanks.

good: Mind the rain on that jacket, it's far too fine to get wet.
Lovely day. Made lovelier by your tailoring, honestly.
Cold, yes. But you look toasty in all that cashmere.
I bet the sun shines a little brighter on people dressed like you.
Bit muggy. Your collar's holding up better than I am.
bad: Weather? You've a car with a driver, what's it matter to you?
Yes, it's raining. Some of us don't own umbrellas with ivory handles.
You look like weather never touches you. It's annoying.
I suppose the weather's different on your side of town.
The clouds don't care what your coat cost.

good: ...Ouch. And from someone who looks like the final word on everything.
That hurts more coming out of a suit like yours.
I... right. I'll go and buy a better shirt, then.
Easy for you to sneer, dressed like a bank. ...It still stings.
Wow. Cut as sharp as your jacket.
bad: Money can buy a suit, not manners.
Insult me all you like. Your cologne's still too strong.
Rich and rude. How original.
Go on, sneer from your silk throne.
I'd care more if I didn't know you've never worked a day.

good: Laugh away, you've clearly earned the right to look down.
...Hah. Yeah. Next to you I do look like a sack of potatoes.
I can't argue with someone that well dressed. I really can't.
That stung. Your whole outfit is mocking me too, isn't it.
Fine. You win. Your shoes already had.
bad: Mock me from inside a thousand-euro suit. Very brave.
Laughing at the poor. Does that come with the cufflinks?
Lovely suit. Shame about the person in it.
I've been mocked by better. Well, cheaper. But better.
Snobbery's the cheapest thing you're wearing.

good: ...You're probably right. You look like someone who's always right.
Hard to argue with a person who clearly has standards.
Alright, alright. Someone dressed like that knows quality.
Point taken. I'll do better. I'll dress better too.
I hate that it sounds true coming out of that collar.
bad: Criticism from somebody who's never ironed their own shirt.
You'd judge a cathedral by its cufflinks.
Keep your standards. They're tailored for you, not me.
Taste isn't wisdom. Remember that.
Your wardrobe has opinions. You needn't share them.

good: ...Alright. People who dress like that have lawyers. And worse.
I believe you. Someone with that much money can make anyone vanish.
No need for that. Please. I know what your sort can afford.
Understood. I'm not crossing anyone with a tailor that good.
Said calmly, in silk. That's the scariest kind.
bad: What, you'll ruin me with your accountant?
Go on, try it. You'd crease your sleeves.
Threats from the champagne crowd. I'm terrified.
You won't do a thing. You'd scuff those shoes.
Money talks. It doesn't scare me.

good: Is that so? You're trouble, in a very expensive suit.
Flirting in a jacket like that ought to be illegal.
Careful, I could get used to the scent of money.
Oh. Me? With you dressed for a royal wedding?
Well. You certainly know how to make an entrance, and an impression.
bad: I'm not for sale, however nice the suit.
Do you flirt with your tailor like that too?
Try that on someone dazzled by cufflinks.
The outfit's charming. The line, less so.
Sorry, I don't date price tags.

good: You're admiring me? I've been admiring your coat for ten minutes.
Coming from someone with your taste, that's a real compliment.
Stop it, this is market stall stuff next to yours.
Admired by a walking runway. I'll dine out on that for a week.
You've an eye for quality. I'm flattered you looked my way.
bad: Look all you like. I'm not one of your acquisitions.
You admire everything you could afford to buy, don't you?
Your gaze comes with a valuation. I can feel it.
Admiration from behind the velvet rope. No, thanks.
I bet you look at paintings the same way. Pricing them.

good: Heavy cream paper, a wax seal... you even write in luxury.
A love letter on stationery like this? I'll keep it forever.
The handwriting's as elegant as the cuffs. I'm melting.
Embossed initials. Oh, you are serious.
I'll read it ten times. And smell the envelope. Is that your cologne?
bad: Gilt-edged paper doesn't make the words true.
Did your secretary write this?
It reads like a contract. A very well-printed contract.
Lovely envelope. Shame it's empty of feeling.
I can't be bought with good stationery.

good: You sing like you dress. Flawlessly.
A serenade from someone in a dinner jacket. I'm in a film.
Was that opera training? Of course it was.
People are staring. Let them, you look magnificent.
Sing it again. I want the whole street to see who's singing to me.
bad: Did you pay someone to teach you that? Ask for a refund.
Nice voice, but you sound like a perfume advert.
Serenading in a tuxedo in broad daylight. Bit much.
All polish, no heart.
Please stop. Your gold watch keeps flashing in my eyes.

good: A dance? I'll try not to crease your silk.
Yes. I've always wanted to dance with someone who looks like a ballroom.
Lead the way. You clearly had lessons.
I'm underdressed, but I'm not saying no.
With you? Everyone in the room will think I'm somebody.
bad: I'm not your arm decoration for the evening.
Dancing's for galas. This is a bus stop.
You'd only be showing off the suit.
No. I'd scuff those polished shoes.
Find a partner who matches your tie.

good: Your hands are so soft. Of course they are.
Oh. Your cufflink's cold. Your hand's warm, though.
I'll hold on. I'm not letting go of something this valuable.
Hand in hand with the best-dressed person here. Look at me.
Careful, people might think I'm rich now.
bad: I'm not something you buy and carry home.
Your rings are digging in. There are too many of them.
That hand's never held a broom, I can tell.
Not here. People will think I'm your latest purchase.
Let go, please. Mine are rough, yours are manicured.

good: Somewhere with tablecloths, I suppose? Yes. Yes, please.
Do I need a new outfit for this? I'll find one.
A date with you? I'll have to borrow my cousin's good shoes.
Yes. Just promise the menu has prices on it so I can faint properly.
Pick me up at eight. In that, ideally.
bad: I'm not going to some restaurant where I can't afford the bread.
Your world isn't mine. I'd feel like a stain on the carpet.
You'd pay for everything and I'd owe you forever. No.
Ask someone who knows which fork to use.
I'm not your charity case for the evening.

good: You... with everything you've got... want me?
I thought you were out of my league. Out of my tax bracket, honestly.
I don't care about the money. But you do look incredible saying it.
I feel the same. I have since I first saw you in that coat.
Say it again, slowly, so I believe someone like you said it.
bad: Feelings aren't something you can buy back, you know.
Pretty words in a pretty suit. I don't trust either.
We live on different floors of the world. It wouldn't work.
I'm sorry. I don't fit in your life. I'd clash with the furniture.
Do you confess to everyone who isn't impressed by your money?

good: ...Your cologne. I'm going to dream about it.
Well. That was as smooth as your silk.
Even your kisses are tailored.
Oh. Kissed by royalty, more or less.
Mind the lipstick on that collar. Actually, don't.
bad: No. I'm not another thing you own.
Back off. You smell like a perfume counter.
Money doesn't entitle you to a kiss.
Kisses don't go on your account.
Wipe off that grin. And half the cologne.

accept: Yes. Draw up the terms, I'm sure you have a lawyer for that.
Agreed. You make everything sound like a sound investment.
Alright. But I'm not changing my wardrobe for you. Well, maybe a little.
You've planned it like a merger. I like it. Yes.
Yes. Someone with your taste wouldn't pick wrong.
reject: That sounds like a clause in a contract, not love.
You negotiate love the way you order suits. No.
Not everything comes in your size.
I'm not signing anything with someone who owns half the street.
No. Your life has too many cufflinks in it for me.

good: A tale about {subject}, told like after-dinner brandy at a private club. Wonderful.
You tell it like you were there. You probably were, first class.
I could listen to that voice for hours. Expensive voice.
Brilliant. Is it true, or did you buy the rights?
Now I know why rich people get invited everywhere.
bad: {subject}? Sounds like yacht party chatter. Boring.
All that polish and the story's still dull.
Another tale of the well-off. Riveting.
Like being read a menu in French. Lovely voice, no point.
Did someone write that for you?

good: A poem about {subject}... recited like a toast at a gala. Beautiful.
Even your rhymes sound hand-stitched.
Gorgeous. Like velvet in my ears.
You recite poetry the way you wear that suit. Effortlessly.
Goosebumps. And in this cheap coat, that's saying something.
bad: {subject}? Pretty. Pretty empty.
Verses for the opera box. I'm in the cheap seats.
Too polished. Poems need a bit of mud on their shoes.
You recited that like you were reading a price list.
Money can buy a poetry tutor. Not a soul.

landGood: Ha! Rich and funny. That's not fair.
Okay, that got me. Didn't think silk suits told jokes.
Hah! Tell that one at your next gala.
I nearly spilled my coffee on your jacket. Sorry!
That's good. Who writes your material, your butler?
landGroan: Oh no. That's a joke your grandfather told at the yacht club.
Groan. An expensive groan, but a groan.
Terrible. You're lucky you're so well dressed.
Ugh. Only someone in that suit could get away with it.
That's an old-money joke. Very old.
flop: ...Was that meant to be funny? I was looking at your shoes.
Silence. Even your joke wears a tie.
I think that one only works in private clubs.
Money can't buy timing, apparently.
Hm. Maybe the punchline's in your other jacket.

good: Thank you. One does try, and the tailor tries harder.
How kind. Most people only praise the coat. You noticed the man inside it.
Praise from someone with an eye. I'll have it pressed and framed.
"Adjusts a gold cufflink." Go on, I'm listening.
Lovely. That's worth more to me than another silk scarf, and I have a drawer of those.
bad: Praise is cheap, darling. I prefer things that come with a receipt.
Mm. I hear that from the doorman every morning, and he's paid to say it.
You said it the way people read a price tag they can't afford.
"Brushes a speck off a lapel." Was that meant to impress me?
Flattery from off the rack. I only wear bespoke.

good: You like it? Casa Ardenzi, autumn line. Only nine were cut.
Finally, someone who can tell cashmere from wishful thinking.
"Smooths the waistcoat." Hand-stitched. Three fittings in Milan. Worth it.
Good taste recognising good taste. How rare in this city.
Thank you. I'll tell my tailor, he lives for news like that.
bad: You complimented the shoes. The shoes are the least of it.
That's last season, darling. Do keep up.
"A thin smile." People who don't know fabric shouldn't comment on it.
Sweet. Wrong, but sweet. It's vicuna, not wool.
I've been complimented by dukes. You'll have to try harder than that.

good: Kind of you. Confidence, like a good suit, is mostly in the shoulders.
You're right. I'll take that meeting, and I'll wear the grey pinstripe.
Encouragement and a decent espresso. That's all one needs, really.
"Straightens a silk tie." Very well. I shall be magnificent.
How generous. I may even tip you for that.
bad: Encourage me? Darling, I own the building.
I don't need a pep talk. I need a better jeweller.
That's the sort of thing they print on cheap greeting cards.
"Checks a gold watch." Are we done with the motivational portion?
People with my bank balance don't get nervous. We get bored.

good: Oh, you're shameless. Do continue, it suits you.
Flattery delivered with conviction. That's practically couture.
"Laughs behind a gloved hand." Too much. Keep going.
I know it's flattery, and I'm paying for it gladly.
Exquisite. You should give lessons to my staff.
bad: I can smell a sales pitch through three layers of cologne.
Darling, the last man who flattered me that hard wanted a loan.
Too obvious. Elegance is knowing when to stop.
"Pockets the wallet a little deeper." Nice try.
That's flattery in polyester. I'll pass.

good: Don't mention it. Truly, it cost me less than these cufflinks.
A thank you, and with manners. You'd do well at a gala.
"A gracious nod." Gratitude looks good on you. Better than that jacket.
My pleasure. Generosity is the only accessory that never dates.
You're welcome. Put it on my tab, everyone does.
bad: Thanks are lovely. A cheque is lovelier.
You say that like you'll forget my name by the tram stop.
"Waves a ringed hand." Yes, yes. Run along.
A thank you in that coat? It loses something.
I was hoping for a gift basket, honestly. Truffles, at least.

good: Charming. Have you been to the new boutique on Via Farini? Criminally expensive. I bought two.
I do love idle chatter. It's the only free thing I enjoy.
"Sips something sparkling." Tell me more, this is delightful.
My yacht's in dry dock, so I have time to talk. Lucky you.
Pleasant. Like a lunch at the club, minus the oysters.
bad: Small talk is for people with small calendars.
"Glances at a gold watch." Fascinating. I have a fitting at three.
Darling, my secretary handles conversations like this.
I've heard livelier talk at a bank vault.
Mm. Do you know who designed this? No? Then we've nothing to discuss.

good: Oh, scandal. My favourite fabric. Do go on.
I heard the same at the opera, but your version has better tailoring.
"Leans in, pearls swaying." And did she wear the green? She did, didn't she.
Delicious. I'll repeat it at the gala as if it were mine.
Gossip and champagne. Now this is how a Tuesday should be.
bad: Darling, that rumour is two seasons old. Like your shoes.
I only trade gossip with people who own a box at the opera.
"Yawns elegantly." I started that rumour myself, actually.
Common people gossiping about common people. How dreary.
That's not gossip, that's a weather report with names.

good: Yes, ghastly rain. I brought the camel coat, thank heavens.
Lovely weather for linen. I wear it whenever the sky lets me.
"Opens a silk umbrella." One must dress for the forecast, darling.
Grey skies, but a cashmere scarf solves most of life's problems.
Indeed. Weather like this is why one keeps a villa on the coast.
bad: I don't notice weather. I have a driver.
The weather? I was born with a winter wardrobe and a summer one. It's never a surprise.
"Brushes rain off a lapel." Must we talk about it?
Darling, only people without umbrellas talk about the rain.
Mm. My suede doesn't care for this topic.

good: "A sharp intake of breath." Nobody has spoken to me like that since boarding school.
How vulgar. And how... accurate. I need to sit down.
That stung through a three hundred euro shirt. Impressive.
I'll have you know this jacket was made for me. By hand. Oh, never mind.
"Clutches the pearls, actually." Well. I never.
bad: Darling, I've been insulted by better-dressed people than you.
Insults bounce off silk. It's in the weave.
"Adjusts a cufflink." Are you finished? Lovely.
My lawyers bill eight hundred euros an hour. Shall we continue?
Say that again, slower, so I can enjoy how cheap it sounds.

good: You mock the hat? The hat cost more than your rent. Oh... that's the joke, isn't it.
"A flush above the silk collar." How terribly unkind.
Laughing at my tailoring. That actually hurt.
I... suppose the gold buckles are a lot. Fine.
Hmph. Mock all you like, I'll still be the best dressed corpse in Bologna.
bad: Mock the coat all you like. It's still worth more than your opinion.
"Laughs, rings glinting." Envy is so unflattering on you, darling.
People laugh at couture until it's in their catalogue next year.
Darling, you can't afford to laugh at me.
Oh, a jester. I'd hire you, but I only employ the well dressed.

good: Too much gold? ...Perhaps. I'll speak to my stylist.
"Looks down at the shoes." Hm. You may have a point about the spats.
Fair. Wealth without taste is just noise, and I've been loud.
That's honest. Nobody on my payroll would dare say it.
Ouch. Very well, the fur collar goes back to the house.
bad: Criticism from that jacket? Bold.
Darling, my taste has been reviewed in three magazines. Yours hasn't.
"Smooths a silk lapel." Noted, and discarded.
You critique me the way a tram critiques a limousine.
I pay people to tell me what's wrong. You're not on the list.

good: "Steps back, polished shoes clicking." Alright, no need to crease anything.
Please, not the suit. Take the wallet, leave the suit.
Fine, fine. Violence is so bad for the fabric.
"A nervous tug at the tie." Let's be civilised about this.
I'll have my driver bring the car around. Somewhere far from you.
bad: Threaten me? I have bodyguards who dress better than you.
"Unimpressed, polishing a ring." Lay a finger on this silk and you'll pay for it. Literally.
Darling, I own your landlord.
Empty threats in a cheap coat. Charming.
I've been threatened by bankers. You're adorable by comparison.

good: Is that so? Say it again, and slower. I like quality.
"Lowers designer sunglasses." You're trouble. Expensive trouble, I hope.
Darling, flirting with me is like window shopping on Via dell'Indipendenza. Dangerous.
Oh, I like you. You're bold, and you almost match my scarf.
Charming. Dinner at eight, and do wear something decent.
bad: Darling, I've been flirted with on three yachts. That was a rowboat.
"Looks you over, top to shoes." No.
Cute. But I only date people with a tailor.
That line was off the rack. Come back with something bespoke.
I'm flattered. And unavailable to anyone in that jacket.

good: You can't stop looking? Understandable. It's the silk.
"Turns slightly, letting the light catch the cufflinks." Better angle?
Admire away. I dressed for exactly this.
How sweet. Most people only stare at the jewellery.
You have a good eye. For coats, and for me.
bad: Darling, staring is for museums. Buy a ticket.
"Covers the watch with a sleeve." Eyes up.
Admiration from a distance, please. This is cashmere.
I'm used to looks. Yours was a little too long.
Mm. Admire the coat. The rest isn't on display.

good: Hand-written, on decent paper. I'm almost moved.
"Reads it with gloved fingers." I'll keep this in the silver box.
Darling, nobody writes letters anymore. Except you. Lovely.
The prose is fine and the envelope is crisp. You've thought about this.
I'll have it sealed in wax and filed with the deeds. That's a compliment.
bad: On lined paper? Darling, honestly.
"Holds it at arm's length." Is this ink or ballpoint?
I receive letters from counts. This reads like a shopping list.
It smells of the tram. I'll pass it to my secretary.
Sweet sentiment, cheap stationery. The two cancel out.

good: A serenade? Under my balcony? How deliciously old money of you.
"Leans on a gilded railing." Again, from the second verse.
Your voice is lovely. Your coat isn't, but your voice is.
I've heard opera at La Scala. That was nearly as good.
Bravo. I'd throw a rose, but they're imported and very dear.
bad: Darling, the neighbours pay a fortune for silence.
"Closes the shutters with a ringed hand." No.
I've had string quartets play at breakfast. That was not a quartet.
Off key and off season. Like your trousers.
Please. My butler sings better, and he's tone deaf.

good: A dance? Mind the shoes, they were cobbled in Florence.
"Offers a gloved hand." Lead well, darling. Everyone is watching.
Charming. I waltz like I spend: with total confidence.
Very well. The orchestra was paid for, we might as well use it.
I accept. Just try to keep up with the hem.
bad: In those shoes? On this marble? Absolutely not.
"Smooths the gown." My card is full. Through next season.
I only dance with people the gala committee has heard of.
Darling, I'd rather not crease anything tonight.
No, thank you. I don't dance below my tax bracket.

good: "Slips off one glove." There. Now you may.
Warm hands. That's worth more than a diamond, almost.
Mind the rings. Yes, all of them. Yes, real.
How old fashioned. I adore old fashioned, it's always in style.
Very well. Hold on tight, I walk fast past the cheap shops.
bad: Not with the kid gloves on, darling. They stain.
"Withdraws a hand heavy with rings." Let's not.
My hands are insured. You'd need to sign something first.
Too soon. I haven't even seen your shoes properly.
Mm. Perhaps after you've had a manicure.

good: Out? Yes. I'll book the table, you'd only choose somewhere with napkins on rolls.
"Checks a leather diary." Thursday. I'll send the car.
How bold. Dress code is jacket and tie. Don't make me regret this.
Lovely. There's a little place by the Two Towers where they know my order.
I accept. You'll get to see me in the evening silk. Lucky thing.
bad: Darling, where would you even take me? A kebab stand?
"Leafs through a leather diary." I'm booked until the next millennium.
I don't go out. Out comes to me.
Not in that coat, and not to anywhere you can afford.
Sweet. No. My standards are imported.

good: Oh. Oh, darling. Nobody has ever wanted me for more than the wallet.
"The gold cigarette case trembles, just a little." Say it once more.
I've bought a great many things. This, I can't buy. I'll treasure it.
Well. I suppose I'll have to clear a wardrobe for you.
You've made me forget what I'm wearing. That has never happened.
bad: Darling, I'm flattered, but feelings aren't in my portfolio.
"Adjusts the tie, avoiding your eyes." Let's pretend you didn't say that.
Everyone confesses once they've seen the villa.
I'm afraid my heart is in a vault, and the combination's lost.
That's very sweet, and very poor timing. My stylist is waiting.

good: "A breath of expensive perfume." Mm. You've earned the second floor of my heart.
Careful with the lipstick, it's French. Oh, never mind. Again.
Well. That was worth the dry cleaning.
Darling. I'll have that framed, if they can frame a moment.
"Smooths a rumpled lapel, smiling." Exquisite.
bad: Not on the silk. Absolutely not on the silk.
"Turns a cheek, diamonds flashing." One does not simply kiss me.
Darling, you've smudged the powder. That took an hour.
Too forward. I'm a gallery, not a market stall.
Mm, no. You taste of the tram.

accept: Agreed. I'll have the terms drawn up on cream paper.
"A slow smile over the champagne flute." Very well. Let's make it elegant.
Yes. And I choose the rings. You'd buy plated.
Darling, that suits us both. Like a jacket cut to measure.
Accepted. My lawyer will be thrilled, he loves a new contract.
reject: No, darling. That arrangement doesn't go with anything I own.
"Closes a jewelled compact." That style is terribly out of fashion.
I don't do bargain arrangements. I do bespoke or nothing.
My lawyers would never allow it, and frankly, neither would my mirror.
Sweet. But I'd sooner wear last year's shoes.

good: A story about {subject}. Well told, with a decent finish. Like a good handbag.
"Sets down the champagne." I'd pay for the sequel. I'd pay well.
Delightful. I'll retell it at the club and claim I was there.
You held my attention longer than my jeweller ever has.
Lovely pacing. Tailored, almost. Bravo.
bad: {subject}? Darling, I've heard that story told better at a charity auction.
"Checks the gold watch twice." Is it nearly over?
Too long, badly cut, loose threads everywhere. Like cheap trousers.
Mm. My chauffeur tells that one. With more style.
The plot was off the rack, darling.

good: A poem about {subject}... exquisite. I'll have it engraved on something silver.
"Presses a silk handkerchief to one eye." Don't look at me, this is cashmere mascara.
Every line fitted perfectly. Like a suit on its fourth fitting.
Bravo. Patrons have funded worse. I may fund you.
Beautiful. Verse like that belongs in a leather binding.
bad: Darling, that rhyme was costume jewellery.
"Polishes a ring instead of listening." Finished?
I've commissioned poets. You'd not make the shortlist.
{subject}, in verse? How very... affordable.
It lacked polish. Everything should have polish.

landGood: "Laughs, pearls bouncing." Oh, that's priceless. And I know prices.
Darling, that was witty. I'll steal it for the gala.
Ha! Careful, I nearly spilt vintage on the silk.
That actually got me. I'd tip you, but you'd only spend it on shoes like those.
Delicious. Humour with tailoring. How rare.
landGroan: Oh, that's dreadful. Tell it again at dinner, the Count will adore it.
"Groans behind a gloved hand." Darling, no. Well, a little yes.
Terrible. Like velvet in August. And yet I'm smiling.
That joke belongs in a bargain bin. I'll take it anyway.
Ugh. Charming, in a cheap sort of way.
flop: ...Was that meant to be funny? It was certainly cheap.
"Adjusts a cufflink in total silence."
Darling, even my butler wouldn't laugh at that, and I pay him to.
That joke was off the rack and badly hemmed.
Mm. Let's never speak of it at the club.

praise: Don't turn around, {name}. I've been watching, and you're good. Genuinely.
I've followed you three streets, {name}. You never once looked lost. I respect that.
From the shadows it's easier to see who's worth it. You are, {name}.
Quietly, so nobody hears: well done, {name}.
I don't come out of the dark for just anyone, {name}. Consider this praise.
compliment: Nice coat, {name}. Easy to pick out in a crowd. Lucky you don't need to hide.
Your footsteps have a rhythm, {name}. I'd know them on any roof in Bologna.
You have good eyes, {name}. You almost spotted me twice.
That's a fine shadow you cast, {name}. I'd borrow it if I could.
I noticed your smile from the alley, {name}. Hard to miss, even in the dark.
encourage: You can do it, {name}. Keep low, keep moving, and nobody stops you.
Breathe slow, {name}. Fear is only noise. Make less of it.
I'll be right behind you, {name}. You won't see me, but I'll be there.
Nobody saw you fail, {name}. Which means you can try again.
Small steps, soft soles, {name}. That's how anything gets done.
flatter: You're the only one in this square I couldn't sneak up on, {name}. Almost.
If I wanted a partner for a night job, {name}, I'd pick you. No question.
Even the cats go quiet when you pass, {name}.
The whole crowd blurs, {name}. You're the one thing I can't stop seeing.
With hands like those, {name}, you'd lift a wallet and leave a thank-you note.
thank: Thank you, {name}. I'll repay it some night when you're not looking.
I owe you one, {name}. You'll never know when I settle it. That's the fun.
Thanks, {name}. Don't mention it. To anyone. Ever.
You helped and didn't ask who I was, {name}. That's worth more than euros.
'A small nod from under the hood' ...Thank you, {name}.
smalltalk: Busy street, {name}. Twelve exits, four blind corners. Not that I counted.
How's your day, {name}? Mine was quiet. I like them quiet.
Funny how no one looks up, {name}. Rooftops are the emptiest place in town.
Been here long, {name}? I have. Since before you arrived.
Do you hear that, {name}? No? Good. Neither does anyone else.
gossip: Heard something through a keyhole last night, {name}. You'll want to sit down.
The baker's not where he says he goes on Thursdays, {name}. I followed.
Walls are thin, {name}, and I'm very good at leaning on them.
Keep this between us and the shadows, {name}: the mayor has a second door.
Nobody saw me, {name}, but I saw everybody. Ask me about the faction captain.
weather: Fog tonight, {name}. My favourite kind of weather.
Full moon, {name}. Terrible for work. Lovely to look at, I suppose.
Rain covers footsteps, {name}. Everyone complains. I say thank you.
Too sunny, {name}. Shadows this short have nowhere to hide anyone.
Clouds rolling in, {name}. By nightfall the streets will be properly dark.
insult: I've been in your house, {name}. Twice. You snore, and your locks are a joke.
You walk like a dropped cutlery drawer, {name}.
I could rob you blind, {name}. I haven't bothered. Think about why.
Your secrets aren't secret, {name}. They're just boring.
You'd lose a game of hide and seek against a lamppost, {name}.
mock: Look behind you, {name}. Ha. Too slow. Always too slow.
Did you hear me coming, {name}? No. You never do.
'Whispers right by their ear' Boo, {name}.
Lovely jingle, {name}. A cat wearing bells would be quieter.
You checked the door three times, {name}. I was inside by the second.
criticize: You talk too loud, {name}. Half the street knows your business.
You leave a trail a child could follow, {name}. Muddy boots, receipts, gossip.
You never check corners, {name}. One day that will cost you.
Your window latch is broken, {name}. Fix it before someone less polite notices.
Stop stomping, {name}. It's the first thing people remember about you.
threaten: You won't see me coming, {name}. That's not a figure of speech.
I know where you sleep, {name}. And which floorboard creaks.
Tonight, {name}, check the shadows in your room. Then check them again.
'A cold blade, briefly, at the back of the neck' We understand each other, {name}?
Next time you blink, {name}, I might not be in front of you anymore.

flirt: I've been watching you all evening, {name}. In the nice way. Mostly.
You caught me looking, {name}. Nobody catches me. Take that as a compliment.
I could disappear right now, {name}. I'd rather stay.
Usually I keep to the dark, {name}. You make me want a lamp.
'Appears at their elbow' Hello, {name}. Miss me?
admire: I've seen a thousand faces from the rooftops, {name}. Yours is the one I looked for.
You move like you own the night, {name}. I'd know.
I memorised your walk, {name}. Purely professional. Mostly.
In the dark everyone looks the same, {name}. Except you.
I stopped watching the street, {name}. I started watching you.
loveLetter: Check your coat pocket, {name}. No, the inside one. I put it there an hour ago.
There's a letter on your pillow, {name}. Don't ask how it got there.
I left you something under your door, {name}. Unsigned. You'll know.
'Slips an envelope into their hand without seeming to move' Read it later, {name}.
Found it in your book, {name}? Page forty. I thought you'd stop there.
serenade: 'Sings very softly, barely a breath' ...It's a quiet song, {name}. For quiet hearts.
From under your balcony, {name}, I'll hum. No one else will ever hear it.
I don't sing loudly, {name}. Lean closer. This one's only for you.
It's an old lullaby thieves sing to the moon, {name}. Tonight it's yours.
'Whistles low from somewhere in the dark' Find me, {name}, and I'll finish it.
askDance: Dance with me, {name}. In the corner, where the lamps don't reach.
I know a rooftop with a view, {name}. No one will see us dance there.
One dance, {name}. I won't step on your feet. I never make a sound.
Shall we, {name}? I'll lead. I'm good at slipping through a crowd unnoticed.
The band can't see us from here, {name}. Let's dance anyway.
holdHands: Give me your hand, {name}. I know the way out. I always do.
Hold on, {name}. Stay in my shadow and nobody will see us.
'Takes their hand so softly they barely notice' There. Was that so hard, {name}?
My hands are usually in other people's pockets, {name}. Yours is nicer.
Stay close, {name}. In the dark, I don't let go.
askOut: Meet me tonight, {name}. Behind the old cinema. Come alone, and don't be followed.
Dinner, {name}? I know a place with a back room and a back door.
Let's go somewhere, {name}. I'll find you. You won't have to find me.
Midnight, {name}, on the bridge. If you can see me, it's a date.
I've never taken anyone out through the front door, {name}. For you I'll try.
confess: I've followed you for weeks, {name}. Not to watch. Because I couldn't stop.
I hide from everyone, {name}. I don't want to hide from you.
Nobody knows I'm here, {name}. I'd like you to be the exception, always.
I've stepped out of the dark for one reason, {name}. It's you.
I keep a lot of secrets, {name}. This is the only one I want to give away: I love you.
kiss: Close your eyes, {name}. I'm very good at being unexpected.
'Steps out of the shadow, right in front of them' Don't move, {name}.
Before the streetlight flickers back on, {name}...
Nobody's watching, {name}. Trust me, I checked.
One kiss, {name}, and then I'm gone. Maybe.
propose: {style}, {name}. Quietly. Nobody else needs to know our arrangement.
I've thought about it in the dark a long time, {name}. I want {style}. With you.
Here's my secret, {name}: {style}. Say yes and I'll stop vanishing.
{style}, {name}. Just a word between two shadows. What do you say?
No one heard me say this, {name}, and no one will: I'd like {style}.

story: I overheard this one through a wall, {name}. It's about {subject}. Lean in.
Lights low, {name}. The story of {subject} only works in the dark.
I was there for {subject}, {name}. Nobody saw me. That's how I know the real version.
Shh. A tale of {subject}, {name}, told the way thieves tell it: quietly.
Everyone knows {subject}, {name}. Nobody knows what happened behind the curtain.
poem: 'Very softly' A small poem, {name}, on {subject}. Whispered, as it should be.
Verses on {subject}, {name}. Written on a rooftop, waiting for a window to go dark.
Shadows have poems too, {name}. This one's about {subject}.
Listen close, {name}. {subject}, in eight quiet lines.
I found this poem on {subject} in a drawer I wasn't meant to open, {name}.

jokes: How many thieves does it take to change a bulb? None. We prefer it dark.
My doctor says I should get out more. I'm out every night. He just never sees me.
I joined a hide and seek club years ago. They're still looking for me.
Why do shadow-walkers never pay at the tavern? Nobody saw them order.
A wizard, a knight and I walk into a tavern. Only two of them get noticed.

good: Gah! Where did you... oh. Thank you, I think.
Kind words from someone I didn't hear walk up. I'll take them.
You crept all the way over here just to say that? Sweet, in a creepy way.
Praise from a shadow. Feels like being knighted by a ghost.
Thanks. Now could you stand somewhere I can actually see you?
bad: Lovely. Now tell me why you were lurking behind the bins.
Praise from a hood with no face in it. No thanks.
Nice try. People who dress like that want something from my pockets.
You appeared out of nowhere to flatter me? I'm counting my wallet.
I'd believe you more if I could see your eyes under all that cloth.

good: Me? Coming from someone who moves like smoke, that's something.
Oh! I didn't even hear you breathe. Thanks, really.
Funny, I didn't think anyone noticed me. But you notice everything, don't you?
A compliment out of the dark. I'll keep it somewhere safe.
You startled me half to death, but thank you.
bad: Says the person dressed like a burglar's shadow.
Don't sneak up on me with compliments. Don't sneak up on me at all.
Hm. What did you lift off me while I was blushing?
Compliments from a hood. Last time I heard that pitch, my bike went missing.
Step into the light and say that again.

good: You really think so? You must have been watching me a while... wait, have you?
Okay. If someone who slips past guards believes in me, I can manage this.
Thanks. I'll try to be as unstoppable as you are unseeable.
Where did you even come from? ...Still, thank you. I needed that.
A pep talk from the shadows. Strangely, it works.
bad: Easy for you to say. You can just vanish when it goes wrong.
Pep talk from a figure in a doorway. Not reassuring.
I don't take advice from people I can't hear coming.
Thanks, ghost. Go haunt somebody else's motivation.
Were you following me to say that? Because that's worse.

good: Oh, stop. And stop doing that silent appearing thing. Actually, keep doing the first one.
Flattery from a phantom. My nan would have fainted.
You noticed all that from the shadows? I'm touched.
Ha! You sneak in and butter me up. Smooth as your footsteps.
Nobody ever sees me. Nice to know a hood does.
bad: Silver tongue, soft shoes. Classic pickpocket kit.
You're laying it on thick. What's behind your back?
People who dress to go unseen shouldn't try so hard to be liked.
Lay off. I can feel you reaching for my coat pocket.
Flattery and a dark hood. I'll keep both hands on my purse.

good: You're welcome. Did I help you, though? I never saw you there.
No need. Just... clear your throat next time before you thank someone.
Anytime. You're the quietest grateful person I've ever met.
Ah! You scared me. But you're welcome.
Think nothing of it. I'll think nothing of where you came from, either.
bad: For what? I don't remember helping anyone in a hood.
Don't thank me. I don't know who you are, and I can't see your face.
Thanks accepted. Now please step out of my shadow.
Mm. People thank me just before I notice something's missing.
Save it. Gratitude from the dark gives me the shivers.

good: Oh, hi. How long have you been standing there? ...Right. Anyway, yes, busy week.
You talk as quietly as you walk. I like it, it's restful.
Small talk with a shadow. Fine, how's the night life? The literal one.
Sure, let's chat. Just don't vanish halfway through a sentence.
Ha, you made me jump. So, what's new in the alleys?
bad: I'd rather not chat with someone who just materialised behind me.
Sorry, I don't do small talk with hoods.
Why are you whispering? Why is everything about you whispering?
Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Are you casing my flat?
You blend in so well I keep losing track of what you said.

good: Oh, you'd hear everything, wouldn't you? Dressed like that, nobody sees you listening.
Ooh. Was that through a keyhole? Don't tell me. Tell me more.
Gossip from the shadows is the best kind. Go on.
How do you know that? ...No, I don't want to know how.
You must hear things even the walls miss.
bad: I don't trade rumours with people who eavesdrop for a living.
So you've been listening at windows. Lovely. What do you know about me?
Keep it. I'm not giving a spy anything back.
That's private. How did you even... no. Go away.
Rumours from a hood are rumours I don't trust.

good: Foggy, yes. Perfect weather for you, I'd say.
Ha, you'd love a moonless night like this. Bet the rain can't even find you.
Overcast. You must feel right at home.
Bit dark out, isn't it? I suppose that's how you like it.
You startled me, but yes, it's turning cold. Good weather for hoods.
bad: Talking about the weather from the shadows. Very normal.
Rain's coming. You'll use it to sneak around, I know your sort.
I don't care about clouds. I care about where you came from.
Pick a sunny spot and stand in it, then we'll talk weather.
Strange to hear about the fog from someone who is basically fog.

good: ...Wait, how long were you behind me, working that one out?
Ouch. Out of nowhere, just like you.
That cut. I didn't see it coming. I didn't see you coming either.
Hey! ...That hurt more than it should. Who are you, anyway?
Right. I'll just go stand somewhere you can't creep up on me.
bad: Insults from a coat rack with a knife. Terrifying.
Brave words for someone who won't even show their face.
Say it in the daylight, shadow.
Pfft. Sneak off, cat burglar.
Whisper louder, I couldn't hear you through the hood.

good: Okay, okay. You've clearly been watching me. That's the worst part.
How do you know I do that? Have you been following me?
Laughed at from the shadows. That stings in a very particular way.
...I didn't think anyone saw that. Wonderful.
Alright, you win. Stop smirking under that hood, I can feel it.
bad: Mock away. You look like you get dressed in a coal cellar.
Very funny, from someone who jumps at their own echo.
Big laugh for a person who has to hide to feel safe.
Go on, giggle. Then crawl back to your alley.
I'd mock you back, but I keep losing you in the shade.

good: You notice every detail, don't you? Fine. I'll fix it.
Hm. Someone who moves like that would know all about sloppiness.
...You watched me do it wrong. Of course you did.
Point taken, quiet one. I'll be more careful.
If the person nobody ever hears says it's clumsy, it's clumsy.
bad: Criticism from a creeper. I'll file it under ignored.
You don't get to judge me from behind a curtain.
Says the one who can't even use a front door.
Show me your face and maybe I'll listen.
Go lurk somewhere else with your notes.

good: ...Okay. I believe you'd do it, and I'd never even hear you.
Please. I'll be sleeping with the lights on as it is.
Fine! Fine. I didn't see anything. I never saw you.
Alright. Now I'll be checking behind every door for a week.
No need. I can guess how quiet that blade is.
bad: Big threat from someone who won't step under a streetlight.
A knife in the dark? I carry a torch, friend.
I've got three locks on my door and a big dog. Try it.
Threats whispered from a hood sound like a bad play.
You'd have to find me first. Oh. Right. Still no.

good: Is that so? You've been watching me from the shadows, haven't you?
Mysterious, quiet and suddenly right next to me. You're trouble.
Didn't hear you come up. Didn't hear my heart either, until now.
Oh. A hood that flirts. I could get used to that.
Slip away later and I might follow.
bad: Sneaking up and flirting? Pick one.
I like to see who I'm flirting with. Lose the hood first.
Hard to swoon when you nearly gave me a heart attack.
No thanks. You'd be gone before breakfast, I can tell.
I don't date people who come in through windows.

good: You noticed me, from wherever it is you hide? That's flattering.
Oh. I thought you only looked at locks and exits.
Admired by someone that hard to see... it feels like a secret.
Admiration in a whisper. That's my favourite kind.
Keep looking. Just let me see you looking back.
bad: So you've been watching me. That's not admiring, that's stalking.
Admire me from the shadows? No. That's unsettling.
I'd rather be admired by someone with a visible face.
How long have you been admiring me from that doorway?
Lovely. Now I'll be checking the alley every night.

good: A letter in my coat? I never felt a thing... that's terrifying and romantic.
It was on my pillow. My door was locked. ...I'm keeping it.
No footsteps, no knock, just this letter. Very you.
You slip notes the way you slip past guards. I love that.
Unsigned, but I knew it was you. Who else moves like that?
bad: How did this get into my locked drawer? I'm calling a locksmith.
A letter that appeared on my nightstand. That's not romance, it's a break-in.
I found it in my pocket and nearly screamed.
Next time, use the post. Like a person.
Love letter or ransom note? I genuinely couldn't tell.

good: You sing as softly as you walk. I had to lean in. I'm glad I did.
A serenade from under my window, in the dark. Of course it is.
That was barely above a whisper and it still got me.
I didn't know shadows could sing. Again, please.
Quiet, low, and just for me. Perfect.
