bad: I can't hear you under the hood. Was that a song?
Singing under my window at midnight? I thought a burglar was humming.
Too quiet. Serenades are meant to be heard, you know.
You hid in the hedge to sing? Come out of the hedge.
Lovely voice. Shame I can't work out where it's coming from.

good: A dance? You'll be light on your feet, I bet. Lead the way.
Yes. You won't step on my toes. You won't even make a sound.
Dancing with a shadow. I'll try to keep hold of you.
Alright, but in the dark corner of the floor. Your choice, I'd guess.
Glide me around, silent one.
bad: Dance? With you vanishing every time the lights dim? No.
You'd slip out halfway through the song, I know it.
I like a partner I can actually see. Pass.
You'd dance in the shadows and I'd dance alone. Not tonight.
Not with someone who moves like they're dodging a guard.

good: Your hand is so quiet. Does that make sense? It feels like a secret.
Okay. Just don't melt into the dark and leave me holding air.
Gloves and all. I'll take it.
Lead me, then. You know all the back ways.
There you are. Hard to lose you now.
bad: No. Last time a stranger in black took my hand, my ring was gone.
Gloved hands out of nowhere? I'll keep mine in my pockets.
I can't even see your face and you want my hand?
Please, step back into the light first.
Let go. I'm checking my rings.

good: A date? Somewhere quiet and dim, I suppose. Yes.
Only if you come to my door. The front door.
Yes. I'd love to see where someone like you goes after dark.
Alright. I'll watch for you. Not that I'll see you coming.
Sure. Dinner on a rooftop? I bet you know every rooftop in town.
bad: Out with you? You'd vanish the moment the bill came.
I don't date people I've only seen from the corner of my eye.
Where would we even go, the sewers?
No. I need someone who uses doors.
You'd stand me up and I'd never know if you came or not.

good: You've been in my shadow this whole time, haven't you? ...I hoped you had.
Of all the secrets you must keep, you told me this one.
I always felt someone watching over me. It was you. Oh.
You stepped out of the dark to say that. That takes nerve.
I love you too, ghost. Stay where I can see you.
bad: I don't even know your face. How can I say it back?
So the footsteps I never heard all month were yours? That's... a lot.
Feelings, from someone who hides everything else? I don't buy it.
I'm sorry. I can't love someone who's never really there.
You've been following me. That's not love.

good: ...I didn't even see you lean in.
Soft as a shadow. Do it again before you vanish.
You lowered your hood for that. I'll remember.
One moment you weren't there. The next, this. Wow.
Mm. Nobody saw that. Nobody ever sees anything with you, do they?
bad: Whoa! Out of nowhere? Don't ambush people with kisses.
The hood got in the way. And I said no.
That's exactly how you'd distract someone to pick their pocket.
No. Step back to where I can see you.
I didn't hear you coming, and I don't want you any closer.

accept: Yes. Whatever we are, it stays between the two of us and the shadows.
You said it out loud. For someone so quiet, that means everything.
Alright. I'll leave the window unlatched for you.
Yes. Just promise you'll come home through the door sometimes.
Agreed. Nobody needs to know, and you'll make sure nobody does.
reject: No. I need someone I can actually find.
You'd keep half of it hidden from me, I know you would.
I can't agree to anything with someone I've never seen in daylight.
No. Go back to the dark, it's better company than I'd be.
Sorry. I won't sign up to be lonely next to a ghost.

good: A story about {subject}, told in a whisper. I held my breath the whole time.
You tell it like you were there, unseen in the corner. Were you?
Gripping. I kept glancing behind me.
So quiet I had to lean in, and I didn't want it to end.
Like a secret you stole from someone. Brilliant.
bad: I couldn't hear half of it under that hood.
A story about {subject}? You mumbled it at the wall.
You trailed off and slipped away before the ending. Typical.
Too hushed. I lost the thread somewhere in the shadows.
Sounds like something you overheard through a keyhole.

good: A poem about {subject}, barely breathed. I felt it more than heard it.
That was like moonlight across a rooftop. Quiet and lovely.
You read it like a secret. I won't tell a soul.
Hushed and sharp. Like a knife you never see.
Again, softer. I didn't know shadows wrote verse.
bad: Was that a poem, or were you muttering to the dark?
I couldn't hear a word. Speak up, ghost.
A poem about {subject}, whispered from a hood. Spooky, not moving.
Every line trailed off, like you were ready to bolt.
Lovely, I'm sure. I'll ask the wall, it was closer.

landGood: Ha! Out of the shadows and straight into my funny bone.
Okay, that got me. Didn't see that one coming either.
Ha! You're funnier than you are visible.
A sneaky punchline. Very on brand.
That snuck up on me. Like you.
landGroan: Oh no. You should have stayed hidden for that one.
Ugh. Creep back into the dark with that pun.
Groan. You whispered it so it'd hurt less? It didn't.
That was awful. And I still laughed under my breath.
Terrible. Go hide. ...Fine, it was a little good.
flop: ...Was that meant to be funny? I couldn't hear it under the hood.
Silence. Fitting, for you.
Even the crickets snuck away from that one.
Was that the punchline? You slipped right past it.
Nothing. That joke vanished faster than you do.

good: Keep it down. ...But thank you. Nobody usually notices me long enough to praise anything.
Mm. Kind words. I'll fold them up and keep them in an inner pocket.
You saw that? Then I was sloppy. Still... it's nice to be seen, once.
"A small nod from under the hood." That's all you get. It means a lot.
Praise from someone who actually spotted me. Rare. I'll allow it.
bad: Louder, why don't you. The whole square can hear where I'm standing now.
Praise is how people get you to stand still. I don't stand still.
You're complimenting a shadow. It doesn't answer to that.
"Steps back into the doorway." No. Too much attention.
Nice try. Flattery is the oldest way to learn someone's face.

good: You like the coat? Charcoal wool. Doesn't catch the streetlights. Good eye.
Soft soles, yes. You noticed the boots. Most people notice the boots too late.
Thanks. I'd smile, but you'd have to find my face first.
Quietly said. That's the only way I take compliments.
Huh. You're observant. I should keep an eye on you... in a good way.
bad: If you can tell what I'm wearing, I'm wearing it wrong.
Compliments draw eyes. Please don't draw eyes.
"Pulls the hood lower." Let's pretend you didn't see the outfit.
You're describing me out loud. Stop describing me out loud.
That's the sort of thing a witness says. I don't like witnesses.

good: Alright. I'll go when the street's empty. Thanks for the push.
You believe I can slip through? Then I'll slip through.
Quiet confidence. I like that. I'll borrow some of yours.
"A brief, almost silent laugh." Fine. Tonight, then. Nobody will know but you.
Good. I needed someone to say it softly. Loud courage gets people caught.
bad: I don't need cheering on. Cheering is noise. Noise gets you found.
Easy for you to say. You've never waited three hours in a coal chute.
Encouragement won't make the floorboards creak less.
Rah rah. Keep your pep talks away from my hiding spots.
I'll move when the shadows say so, not when you do.

good: "Something in the dark might be blushing." ...Don't look.
Unseen by the best guards in Bologna? Well. Maybe one or two.
You flatter like a cat burglar works. Smooth, light, gone before I notice.
Mm. Sweet. Say the rest in a whisper.
I don't hear that often. Mostly because nobody knows I was there.
bad: Butter for the guard dog. I've used that trick myself.
Too sweet. People sweeten the words when they want a name.
"Slips half a step out of reach." Whatever you're selling, I wasn't here to buy it.
Flattery is just a loud way of fishing. I don't bite.
Funny. That's exactly what the last informant said.

good: No need. Just don't mention to anyone that I helped.
"A quick nod, already turning to the alley." You're welcome.
Glad it worked. Forget my face, that's thanks enough.
Thanks received. Quietly. The way it should be.
Mm. Owe me nothing. Or owe me a back door, someday.
bad: Thanks for what? I was never here.
Don't thank me in the street. People remember who gets thanked.
Gratitude leaves tracks. Wipe yours.
"Already gone by the time you finish the sentence."
Keep it. If anyone asks, you did it alone.

good: Fine. Small talk. Lower your voice and stand by the wall, we'll look like nothing.
Not much new. Two new guards on the bridge, a loose drainpipe on Via Rizzoli. Usual.
Quiet day. I like quiet days. Nobody looks up.
Mm, sure. I'll chat. Just keep your back to the window.
You talk, I'll listen. Listening is what I'm good at.
bad: Chatting in the open. This is how people end up on wanted posters.
I don't do small talk. Small talk is how people learn your accent.
"Silence. When you look back, the spot is empty."
Nothing to say. Saying things leaves a trail.
Weather, family, work... I'm not giving you any of it.

good: Oh, I've heard. I hear everything from the rafters. Lean closer.
That one? Old news. Want the version nobody else knows?
"A whisper, barely a breath." The baker's been meeting a wizard behind the tram depot.
Gossip is just intelligence with bad manners. Go on.
I was in the room when that happened. Nobody saw me, naturally.
bad: Shh. Walls have ears. I know, I'm usually one of them.
I trade secrets. I don't give them away in the street.
Sloppy rumour. Whoever told you that was standing in plain view.
No. If I repeat it, they'll know who heard it.
Gossip is how people get followed home. I'd know.

good: Fog tonight. Lovely. Nobody sees anyone in fog.
Overcast, no moon. My kind of weather.
Rain's good. Covers footsteps, washes away tracks.
Mm. Long evenings in autumn. More dark to work with.
Yes, cloudy. The streetlamps look like lonely little moons. I like that.
bad: Full sun. Everyone casts a shadow. Even me. Terrible.
Clear skies and a bright moon. Worst week of the year.
Fresh snow? Every step a signature. No thank you.
I don't care about the weather. I care about the lighting.
"Glances at the sky, then at the exits." Not tonight.

good: ...Fine. Noted. I'll be somewhere you can't see me. Which is anywhere.
"The hood dips, and for a moment they seem smaller."
That stung. Don't expect to hear me coming next time. Or ever.
Hm. Well. I'll go and be invisible somewhere less rude.
You found the soft spot. Most people can't even find me.
bad: Insult someone you can actually find tomorrow.
"A soft laugh from somewhere to your left. Weren't they on your right?"
Words. I've heard worse whispered through keyholes.
Go ahead. I'm already gone in your memory.
Shout it if you like. You'll be shouting at an empty doorway.

good: ...Alright, the cape snagged on one fence. Once.
"Silent, but the shoulders tense under the dark cloth."
Low blow. Quiet, but low.
Fine, laugh. I'll remember it from very close by.
Hm. I'd hide my face, but it's already hidden.
bad: Mock away. You won't remember where I was standing.
Funny. You're laughing at a coat. I left it there for you.
"Not a flinch. Not a sound. Then a step back into the dark."
Cute. The guards laughed at the black cat too, before the vault was empty.
Yes, very amusing. Check your pockets.

good: ...You're right. I was heard on the stairs. It won't happen again.
Fair. I've been getting careless. Too many easy rooftops.
"A long, quiet exhale." Point taken. I'll work on it in the dark.
Hm. Nobody tells me that. Nobody sees enough to tell me that.
I'll fix it. Quietly, like everything else.
bad: Criticism from someone who walks in boots like that? Please.
You couldn't even tell I was behind you an hour ago.
"Says nothing. Says nothing for a very long time."
Tell me how to vanish when you've learned to.
Noted, and ignored. Silently.

good: ...Alright. Alright. I'll go. You won't see me again.
"Already backing into the shadows, palms open."
No need for that. I know when to be somewhere else.
Understood. I was never here, and I'm leaving.
Fine. You win this street. I have others.
bad: Threaten me? You'd have to find me first.
Brave words for someone who doesn't know where I sleep. I know where you sleep.
"The lamp flickers. When it steadies, they're behind you."
Go on. I'll be the draught at your neck tonight.
Loud. Very loud. I prefer to answer quietly, later.

good: Careful. I'm hard to catch. ...Though you're doing alright.
"A smile, just visible under the hood." You noticed me. That's flirting already.
Say that again. Softer. Like a secret.
You're trouble. Quiet trouble. My favourite kind.
Hm. Maybe I'll let you see where I disappear to.
bad: Flirting in public? Everyone's looking now. Thanks.
I don't get caught that easily.
"One blink, and the spot they stood in is empty."
Too loud. Romance should be whispered.
You're flirting with a silhouette. It's not going to flirt back.

good: You've been watching me? Usually that's my job.
Admire away. Few people ever get to see me long enough.
"Lingers in the lamplight a second longer than they should."
Mm. I'll let you look. Just this once. Don't tell anyone.
That's... nice. Being seen on purpose.
bad: Stop staring. Staring is how guards notice a shape.
If you can admire me, I'm doing something wrong.
"Steps out of the light." Better.
Admire the dark, then. That's where I'll be.
Eyes elsewhere, please. You're giving away my position.

good: A letter slipped into my coat without me noticing? ...I'm impressed. And charmed.
I'll read it by the light of a single match. Then burn it. And remember every word.
No signature? Clever. I knew it was you anyway.
"Folds it very small and hides it somewhere secret."
Written words, delivered quietly. You speak my language.
bad: A letter is evidence. Do you know what you've handed me?
You signed it. With your full name. Oh dear.
"The letter is back in your pocket before you notice. Unopened."
Paper trails get people hanged. Take it back.
Sweet, but I don't keep things that can be found.

good: Softly, please. ...Yes, like that. Just for me.
"Listens from the dark of the balcony, perfectly still."
A song nobody else can hear. That's the most romantic thing there is.
Mm. Hum it again. Quieter. I want it to be ours.
Lovely. And somehow you didn't wake the whole street.
bad: You're singing. Outside. At night. Every window just opened.
Please stop, half of Bologna knows where I'm standing now.
"The balcony is empty before the second verse."
A serenade is a flare with a melody. No.
Beautiful voice. Terrible place to use it.

good: A dance? In the corner, where the light doesn't reach. Yes.
I move quietly. Try to keep up.
"Takes your hand without a sound and leads you into the shadows."
Fine. One dance. Nobody will remember we were on the floor.
Slow steps, soft shoes. You'll like dancing with me.
bad: In the middle of the floor? Under the chandelier? Absolutely not.
Dancing is being looked at with music. Pass.
"You turn to offer your hand. Nobody is there."
I don't dance where people watch. That's everywhere.
Ask me again in a room with no windows.

good: "Gloved fingers close around yours, quiet as a lock clicking."
Alright. But we walk in the shade.
Warm hands. Mine are always cold from waiting in doorways.
Mm. Nobody gets this close to me. Hold on, then.
Keep holding. If I vanish, you're coming with me.
bad: You reached for me and caught air. That's on purpose.
Not here. Hands are how people get grabbed.
"The hand you were holding is suddenly just a glove."
I keep my hands free. Always. Sorry.
Too fast. I'm the one who decides who gets close.

good: Yes. Somewhere dark. A cinema, back row. I'll find you.
Alright. Don't wait at the door, I'll already be inside.
"A whisper at your ear." Tomorrow, after midnight. The old bell tower.
A date. With me. You know you won't see me arrive, right?
Mm. I'll pick the place. You won't find it without me.
bad: A restaurant with big windows on the piazza? Never.
Out? I don't go out. I go through.
"No answer. Just the faint sound of a window latch, somewhere."
Dates leave witnesses. Waiters, mostly.
Not yet. I don't know if I can trust you with where I'll be.

good: ...I knew. I hear everything. I just wanted you to say it.
"For once, they step fully into the light." Me too.
You found the one secret I couldn't steal. I feel the same.
Shh. Say it once more, quietly. I'll keep it hidden forever.
I've been following you for weeks. ...That came out wrong. I mean yes.
bad: Feelings make people careless. I can't be careless.
I'm sorry. I'm better at disappearing than at this.
"Listens to every word. Then, gently, isn't there anymore."
You'd be in love with someone you've barely seen. Think about that.
That's not a secret I can carry. Too heavy, too loud.

good: "A kiss in the dark, so quick and quiet you'll wonder if it happened."
Mm. Nobody saw that. Good.
You caught me. Not many can say that.
Again, before the streetlamp comes back on.
That one I'll keep. Somewhere nobody will ever find it.
bad: Too close, too fast. I'm out of reach on reflex.
"You lean in. There's only a draught and an open window."
Not in the open. Never in the open.
I don't let people corner me. Even nice ones.
Close. But nobody gets that close to me yet.

accept: {style}. Yes. Let's keep it quiet, but yes.
"A whispered answer, warm against your ear." {style} suits us.
Agreed. {style}, and nobody else needs to know the details.
{style}... I'd been planning my exit. I'll stay instead.
Fine. {style}. I'll still vanish sometimes, but I'll always come back.
reject: {style}? That's a lot of daylight for someone like me.
No. {style} means being found every night. I can't promise that.
"They're gone before the word {style} has finished echoing."
I don't sign up for anything. Not even {style}.
Not {style}. Not yet. I still keep a bag packed by the window.

good: {subject}... I love a story told in a low voice. Keep going.
"Listens from the shadow of the archway, utterly still." Good story.
The part about {subject} sneaking past the guards? Accurate. Trust me.
Mm. You tell it like a whisper. That's the right way.
I'll remember that one. Nobody saw me listening, which makes it better.
bad: Too loud. A story about {subject} should be told in the dark.
The hero just walked through the front door? Amateur.
"Somewhere around the second act, the listener is no longer there."
Nobody could hide like that in {subject}. I'd know.
You gave everything away in the first line. No mystery at all.

good: A poem about {subject}... quiet, like footsteps on velvet. Beautiful.
"A soft breath out, almost a sigh." Read it again. Lower.
Short lines, lots of silence between. That's how I'd write it.
Lovely. I'll fold it up in my head and hide it.
Mm. Poems are just secrets with rhythm. That was a good one.
bad: Recited like a town crier. Poems should be murmured.
{subject}? Every line rang like a dropped key.
"Slips away between the second and third stanza."
Too much rhyme. Rhyme is predictable. Predictable gets caught.
Nice words, but you said them to the whole street.

landGood: "A small, muffled snort from under the hood." Okay. That was good.
Ha... shh. I almost laughed out loud. Do you know how dangerous that is?
That one got through my guard. Not many things do.
Mm. Funny. I'll steal it.
"Shoulders shaking, perfectly silent." ...Don't look at me.
landGroan: Ugh. That joke should hide somewhere and never come out.
"A quiet groan, swallowed fast." Fine. Fine.
Terrible. I'll pretend I wasn't here for it.
I'd vanish if I could. Oh, wait. Give me a moment.
That pun creaked like a bad floorboard. ...I liked it anyway.
flop: ...I'm not even here. Neither is your punchline.
"Silence. The kind I'm good at."
That joke left fewer traces than I do.
Was that a joke? It snuck past me completely.
Hm. I've heard louder laughs from an empty corridor.

praise: Good work, {name}. I don't say that often. Most people I talk to are not still standing.
"Rests a spiked gauntlet on your shoulder, gently." Well done. Truly.
You did that well, {name}. I've crushed men who did worse with more.
Respect, {name}. And I keep my respect in the same place I keep my axe: close.
That was strong work. Strong enough that I'd {rather have you beside me|not want you across from me}.
compliment: Nice coat, {name}. Would be a shame if it ever got blood on it. Not yours, I mean.
You've got steady hands. I notice hands. Mostly when they reach for weapons.
"Visor creaks up." You have kind eyes, {name}. Rare, where I usually stand.
That's a good look on you. Brave, wearing so little iron around me.
Your voice is calm, {name}. People usually stammer by now. I like that.
encourage: Get up, {name}. Fear is just pain that hasn't arrived yet. Walk through it.
You can do this. I've seen men do worse things with fewer limbs.
Go on. If anyone stops you, tell them who's standing behind you. Then point.
"Thumps chestplate." Courage, {name}. Borrow some of mine. I have spare.
Don't flinch. Flinching is for the ones who meet me at night.
flatter: {name}, you're the only person in this square I wouldn't break first. Take that as high praise.
Clever and fearless. If you ever need a wall of iron at your back, I'm the wall.
You're too good for this street, {name}. Say a name and I'll make it smaller.
Honestly? You're the most dangerous one here. After me. Well behind me.
"Sheathes the cleaver, slowly." For you, I put the blade away. Nobody gets that.
thank: Thank you, {name}. I'll remember this. I remember everything, good and bad.
You helped me. That makes you mine to protect now. Anyone touches you, they answer to the spikes.
"A heavy nod, armour grinding." I owe you. I always pay my debts. In full.
Thanks. Next time someone gives you trouble, just say my name loudly.
Grateful, {name}. Truly. Usually people only do me favours out of fear.
smalltalk: Quiet day, {name}. Nobody's tried to stab me since breakfast. I almost miss it.
Had my plate polished this morning. The smith wouldn't look me in the eye. Sweet man.
So. What do you do, {name}? I mostly stand in doorways until people leave.
"Leans on a war maul the size of a lamppost." How's the family? All in one piece?
Bus driver let me ride free again today. Didn't even ask. People are so generous.
gossip: Heard the baker's been shorting people. I went in to ask. He's very generous now.
Word is someone's been spreading tales about me, {name}. You wouldn't know who? No? Good.
The Vasari brothers owe half of Bologna money. Owed. They've settled up. Ask me how.
That loud fellow from the bar moved to Modena. Overnight. Funny, the timing.
"Lowers voice to a growl." The council's scared of someone. I hope it's me.
weather: Rain again, {name}. Rusts the spikes. Means I have to sharpen them more. Not complaining.
Hot one. Plate armour in this sun is a slow oven. Builds character. And temper.
Fog's rolling in. Good weather for people to hear me before they see me.
Lightning tonight. I like storms. They're the only thing louder than me walking in.
Cold enough to freeze the blood. Most blood around me goes cold early anyway.
insult: You're a disappointment, {name}, and I've buried better.
"Looks down from a great height." I've met rats with more spine than you.
Your face would improve with a dent. I've got just the gauntlet.
{name}, you're not worth the effort of the swing. And I swing at everything.
Pathetic. I've seen braver things squirming under my boot.
mock: Oh, look at you, all puffed up. Like a pigeon. I eat pigeons, {name}.
"Laughs, a sound like a portcullis dropping." That's your tough face? Adorable.
Shaking, {name}? It's only me. I'm not even holding the big axe yet.
Brave little {name}. Say something else clever. I'll wait. I've got all day and spikes.
You call that a weapon? I pick my teeth with bigger.
criticize: Sloppy, {name}. On a battlefield, sloppy gets you a short funeral.
Your stance is weak. Anyone could knock you flat. I could do it with a sneeze.
You talk too much and act too little. Iron doesn't care about speeches.
That plan has more holes than my last opponent. And he had a lot.
Soft, {name}. Everything about you is soft. Harden up or get broken.
threaten: "Draws a blade as long as your leg." Say that again, {name}. Slowly.
Walk away now, and you keep all your teeth. That's my best offer.
I know where you sleep, {name}. I know where everyone sleeps.
One more word and they'll need a mop, not a doctor.
"Skull pauldrons rattle." These used to belong to people who argued with me.

flirt: {name}, you're the first thing in years that made my heart beat faster than a fight.
"Lifts the visor." I don't take this off for just anyone. Look all you like.
I could break anyone in this square. I'd rather walk you home, {name}.
You're not scared of me. That's either very stupid or very attractive. Maybe both.
I've charged cavalry lines with less nerve than it takes to talk to you.
admire: You've got a fire in you, {name}. I know fire. I've walked out of a few.
"Stops polishing the war axe to stare." Sorry. You're worth putting the blade down for.
Strong jaw, steady gaze. You'd look good on a battlement, {name}.
You carry yourself like someone who's never been afraid. I'd like to keep it that way.
I've seen fortresses fall. Nothing's struck me as hard as you just did.
loveLetter: "Hands over a letter sealed with a skull-shaped wax stamp." Read it. Don't laugh.
I wrote this by candlelight, {name}. Snapped three quills. Gauntlets aren't made for poetry.
Here. It says things I can't say out loud without frightening the pigeons.
"Slides a folded page across, pinned by a dagger." The dagger's a gift too.
Took me all night. The ink's a little smeared. Some of that might be rust.
serenade: "Booms out a war ballad, softened as much as a war ballad can be." This one's for you, {name}.
I only know battle hymns. So imagine you're the hill I'd die defending.
"Beats time on a shield." Oh {name}, my heart's an iron gate, and you've got the key...
My voice cracks glass, they say. Tonight it'll crack only for you.
The last time I sang, a whole regiment ran. Don't run, {name}. Please.
askDance: Dance with me, {name}. I promise I'll take the spiked boots off first.
"Offers a gauntleted hand." I'll lead. Nobody ever argues when I lead.
The floor clears when I walk on it. Plenty of room for two.
I can swing a greatsword in rhythm. A waltz can't be much harder.
One dance, {name}. If anyone stares, they stop staring. I'll see to it.
holdHands: "Slowly pulls off a spiked gauntlet." Here. The real hand. Hold it.
Your hand's so small in mine, {name}. Don't worry. I know exactly how hard to squeeze.
This hand has broken doors. Right now it only wants to hold yours.
Take it. Nobody will bother us. Nobody ever bothers me.
Careful of the knuckle spikes. I'll turn them inward, for you.
askOut: Dinner, {name}. Anywhere you like. They'll find us a table, they always do.
Come to the fights with me Saturday. Ringside. Nobody ever sits next to me, so there's room.
"Clears throat like a drawbridge lowering." Will you go out with me? Say yes. Please.
There's a trattoria on Via Zamboni. The owner owes me. Best seats in the house.
Tomorrow night, you and me, the old walls by moonlight. Bring a coat, I'll bring the axe.
confess: {name}. I've faced trolls, sorcerers, a whole tax office. Nothing scares me like telling you this. I love you.
"Kneels, plate armour hitting the ground like thunder." I'm yours. Every spike of me.
I came into this world swinging. Then I met you and forgot how to make a fist.
Everyone fears me. I only fear one thing: you saying no.
My heart's under three inches of steel, {name}. Somehow you got to it anyway.
kiss: "Lifts the horned helm off and leans in, very slowly."
Close your eyes, {name}. You won't see the skulls that way.
"Drops the war maul with a crash and pulls you close."
I've never been gentle in my life. Let me try now.
Come here, {name}. Mind the spikes.
propose: {name}. {style}. That's how it'll be between us, and I'll fight anyone who says otherwise.
"Drives the axe into the floorboards." {style}, {name}. I swear it on this blade.
I don't do half measures. {style}, {name}. Say yes and the whole street will know to respect it.
Here's my terms, {name}: {style}. Fewer terms than I give most people. Kinder ones too.
{style}. I've held castles on less certainty. Will you hold it with me, {name}?

story: Sit, {name}. This is the tale of {subject}. It ends with a lot of broken shields.
"Plants a greatsword in the ground like a lectern." {subject}. Listen, and don't interrupt.
{subject}. I heard it from a man I was holding over a bridge. He told it very quickly.
They say {subject} is a children's story. Not the way I tell it. Not with this much blood.
Let me tell you about {subject}, {name}. Every word true, and anyone who says otherwise meets my axe.
poem: "Clears throat, gravel rolling." A poem. On {subject}. Iron rhymes with iron, that's the rule.
{subject}... O, steel and ruin, skull and crown, I walk, and cities kneel down.
I wrote this about {subject} between two duels. Bear with the scansion, the second duel ran long.
{subject}. Short poem. Like most of the men who interrupted it.
For you, {name}, verses on {subject}. Read aloud in a voice that shakes windows.

jokes: Why don't skeletons fight me? They've seen what I wear on my shoulders.
A bandit asks me for my money or my life. I asked him which of his he'd rather keep.
How many of me does it take to change a lamp? None. The room just stays dark out of respect.
My smith asked if I wanted the spikes sharper. I said no, I want people to see them coming. Slowly.
A man told me to smile more. So I did. He moved to Sicily.

good: Praise from someone wearing that many skulls... I'll take it, thank you.
Oh. Oh good. I thought the axe was coming out.
Coming from you? I'll sleep better knowing you approve of me.
Thank you! Please don't change your mind, I like my teeth where they are.
Spikes on your knuckles and kind words in your mouth. Odd mix. Nice, though.
bad: Nice words, but your hand hasn't left that hilt once.
Praise is cheaper than plate, and I can tell which one you spent more on.
I'd believe it more if your helmet wasn't grinning at me.
That's what the butcher says to the lamb, isn't it?
Hard to feel flattered with all those spikes pointed my way.

good: A compliment, from... that. I'm going to tell my mother.
Thanks. I'll admit I flinched first, then I blushed.
You noticed my coat? I was too busy noticing your skull pauldrons.
Huh. The big scary one thinks I look good. Today's turning around.
{Thanks|Cheers}. Say it again, quieter, so the chains stop rattling.
bad: Sounds like something you say right before taking my wallet.
Every compliment sounds like a ransom note coming through that visor.
Thanks, I suppose. Could you lower the hammer while you're being nice?
I can't hear compliments over the clanking, sorry.
Your mouth says nice, your gauntlets say ten seconds to run.

good: If someone built like a siege tower says I can do it... fine, I can do it.
Right. Yes. I'll try harder, mostly so you don't come back to check.
That's oddly motivating. Like a drill sergeant made of iron.
With you in my corner, who's going to argue?
You'd make a great coach. Nobody would dare quit.
bad: Easy for you to say, you've got half a forge strapped to you.
Encouragement from a walking warning sign. Pass.
I feel less encouraged, more conscripted.
Is that a pep talk or an order? With the spikes it's hard to tell.
Not everyone can solve problems by looming over them.

good: Flattery from somebody in skull plate. I'm framing this moment.
Stop it, you'll make me forget to be terrified.
Ha! Nobody dares flatter you, so I'll enjoy being flattered by you.
I'll take it. Saying no to that greatsword seemed rude anyway.
That's sweet. Terrifying, but sweet.
bad: Butter on a blade is still a blade.
You're laying it on thicker than that armour.
I know a shakedown when it's wearing spikes.
Flattery doesn't suit a face hidden behind horns.
Smooth words from a rough helmet. I don't buy it.

good: You're welcome! Really, any time, please remember I was helpful.
A thank you from you is worth more than a bodyguard.
Glad to help. Glad to still be standing, too.
No trouble at all. Tell your friends I'm on your side.
Wow. I didn't know that much iron could say thank you.
bad: Gratitude sounds strange through a skull-faced visor.
Thanks for what? I only helped because of the axe.
Don't thank me, just stop following me with that mace.
Right. I'll consider us even, from a safe distance.
Polite words, bloody knuckles. I'll keep my distance.

good: Ha, you're chattier than your spikes suggested.
Turns out the walking fortress has opinions on bus timetables.
Nice to just talk. Everyone else has fled the square, have you noticed?
I was ready to hand over my wallet, and instead we're talking about soup.
You know, under all that plate you're quite ordinary. In a good way.
bad: Sorry, I can't make small talk with someone carrying an axe that big.
Mm. Yes. Lovely. May I go now?
Every pause in this conversation feels like you deciding something.
I'd chat, but your helmet keeps staring at me.
Small talk, big hammer. I'll pass.

good: Ooh, people tell you everything, don't they? Fear loosens tongues.
Really? Well, I won't be the one to cross whoever told you.
Who'd dare lie to your face? That rumour must be true.
Ha! And they still owe you money? Poor fools.
I'm keeping quiet about this. Mostly because you told me to.
bad: I'm not passing that on, I don't want it traced back to the spiky one.
Gossip from you sounds like a list of future victims.
No thanks. Knowing what you know seems dangerous.
I'd rather not hear who's on your bad side.
Rumours from someone dressed like a massacre? I'll check elsewhere.

good: True. Must be murder in all that iron in this heat.
Ha, you'd make a fine lightning rod in this storm.
Rain beading off the spikes like that. Almost pretty.
Mild, yes. Mild compared to standing near you.
Does your armour rust? Sorry, I'm genuinely curious now.
bad: The forecast round you is always a chance of blood.
Could you discuss the weather without resting your hand on the axe?
It's cold, yes. Colder since you walked over.
Weather? I'm too busy watching your hammer.
The sky's fine. It's you that looks like a storm.

good: Alright, alright! I'm hideous, whatever you say, just keep that thing sheathed.
...From someone that size, that one actually hurt.
I'll go home and think about it. Far from here.
Fair enough. I'm not arguing with the skulls.
Right. Noted. Please stop looming.
bad: All that steel and the best you've got is that?
Big armour, small vocabulary.
Insults don't get scarier with spikes on them.
I've been called worse by people in far less plate.
Your blacksmith works harder than your wit.

good: Laugh all you like, I'm not laughing back at that helmet.
Ha... yes, very funny. I'll just shrink a bit, shall I?
Okay, that stung. And everyone's looking, because you're terrifying.
Fine, I'm a joke. You're a siege engine. Point taken.
Mock away. With that cleaver on your back, I'm not risking a comeback.
bad: Mocking me from inside a tin can covered in horns? Bold.
You look like a nightmare and laugh like a goat.
Is the armour compensating for the jokes?
Go on, laugh. Your helmet does the talking better.
I'm not scared enough to find that funny.

good: You're right, you're right. I'll fix it before you come back.
Criticism from someone carrying a war maul tends to stick.
Point taken. Please don't take anything else.
Okay. I'll do better. I'd like to stay unflattened.
Harsh. True, but said by a horned helmet, so extra harsh.
bad: Says the one dressed like a scrap yard with a grudge.
Criticise my work once you've put down the cleaver.
You want to know what's wrong? Fine. Your armour clashes.
I don't take notes from walking armouries.
Spiky opinions, not sharp ones.

good: Okay! Okay. Whatever you want, it's yours.
I believe you. I believed you before you opened your mouth.
No need, no need. Look, my hands are empty, unlike yours.
...I'm going to walk away very slowly now.
You didn't even have to say it, the skulls said it.
bad: The armour's scary. The threat isn't.
Go on then. In plate that heavy, you'll never catch me.
I've seen scarier outfits at the carnival in Venice.
Threats are all shout and spikes. I'm not moving.
My uncle wears more iron than that to fix the boiler.

good: Dangerous and flirty. My mother warned me about your kind.
Ooh. I'm terrified, and also somehow into it.
Do the spikes come off for a date, or...?
You make my heart race. Half of it is fear, but still.
Careful, I like the ones who look like trouble in full plate.
bad: Hard to flirt back while I'm planning an escape route.
That sounded more like a hostage negotiation.
No thanks. I like my dates without blood on the gauntlets.
Was that a wink? I can't tell under the visor.
I'd blush, but all my blood has gone to my legs, ready to run.

good: Me? You're the one who stops traffic. Literally, people swerve.
Admired by a walking fortress. That's a first.
Keep looking at me like that and I'll forget about the battleaxe.
Thank you. Your skulls are lovely too. Is that weird? That's weird.
From someone that fearsome, that look means a lot.
bad: Please stop staring. It feels like you're picking a target.
Admiring me, or sizing me up for the axe?
That gaze through the eye slits is giving me chills. Bad ones.
I'd prefer to be admired by something without horns.
I can feel your stare through two inches of steel. Stop.

good: A love letter... in such neat writing, from such enormous gauntlets.
There's a bloodstain on the corner, but the words are sweet.
You wrote this? You, with those spiked fists? I'm keeping it forever.
Nobody would dare send me another one now. Fine by me.
I'll read it again tonight. Behind a bolted door, out of habit.
bad: It reads like a ransom note with hearts drawn on it.
Is that wax seal a skull? It is. I'm not opening it.
I'm not sure whether to answer it or hide from it.
Lovely penmanship. Terrifying postman.
I'll keep it, mostly because I'm afraid to throw it away.

good: That voice came out of that armour? I'm stunned.
You sang and the chains kept time. Strangely beautiful.
Even the dogs stopped barking. Out of fear, but they did.
A war cry turned love song. I'm melting.
Beautiful. Sing again, only maybe put the mace down first.
bad: That sounded like a battle hymn for burning villages.
Your helmet made it echo like a dungeon.
Was that a song or a warning?
The neighbours have bolted their shutters, if you're wondering.
Please stop, the whole street thinks it's under siege.

good: Dance with the scariest thing in the room? At least nobody will cut in.
Yes. Just mind the spikes on the turn.
Lead the way. The floor's already cleared itself for you.
I'd love to. Try not to step on me in those iron boots.
A dance! The band won't dare stop playing.
bad: In that plate? You'll crush my feet to paste.
I'm not dancing with something that clanks.
One twirl and those spikes take my eye out. No.
Let's not. The floorboards won't survive you.
Dance? I'd rather keep both my arms.

good: Your gauntlet's freezing, but gentle. Who knew?
I've never felt safer. Nobody's coming near me now.
Okay. Holding hands with a war machine. Sure. Yes.
Mind the knuckle spikes... ah, there. That's nice.
Nobody in this town will bother me again, will they?
bad: My fingers! Those knuckle spikes are not decorative!
It's like holding hands with a bear trap.
Let go, please, I can feel the rivets.
Not until you take off whatever that is with the barbs.
I'd rather not be led anywhere by something that dangerous.

good: Yes. Somewhere with a very sturdy chair, please.
A date with you? We'll get the best table in town. The staff will make sure.
Sure. Nobody's going to mug us, that's for certain.
Alright, but you're the one telling my father.
I'd love to. Wear the horns, I want to see the waiter's face.
bad: Where, the battlefield? No thank you.
I'm busy. For the rest of the year. Sorry.
Every trattoria in Bologna would empty the moment you walked in.
A date with you sounds like a hostage situation with candles.
Ask again without the war hammer and maybe.

good: All that iron, and inside, this? Oh, come here. Carefully.
You were scared to tell me? You? I'm touched.
I think I feel the same. The fear wore off and something else stayed.
A heart behind the skull plate. I knew it.
Say it again. Nobody believes the terrifying one has feelings.
bad: That's... a lot of feeling from a lot of armour. I need space.
I'm flattered, and also scared you'll take no badly.
Please don't be upset. Please really, really don't be upset.
I can't. I keep picturing the axe.
Let's stay friends. Distant friends. Friends across a river.

good: I expected cold steel. You're warm, actually.
Worth the bruise from the helmet.
Kissed by a legend of terror. My friends won't believe it.
Oh. Everyone saw that, and nobody will dare say a word.
Gentler than I expected from someone carrying a cleaver that size.
bad: Ow! Your visor! My nose!
I'm not kissing anything with tusks on its helmet.
Back up, your spikes are in my ribs.
That felt like being headbutted by a fortress.
No. Not while the axe is still in your other hand.

accept: With you? Yes. Who'd dare object?
Fine, yes. And anyone with a problem can take it up with your sword.
Yes, that's how we'll be. And nobody will ever bother us.
I'll agree. Not because I'm scared. Mostly not.
Yes. Let's tell the town and watch them all nod very quickly.
reject: I don't make vows to someone in battle dress.
No. I'm not agreeing to anything at axe point.
That sounded like terms of surrender, not a proposal.
Ask me again out of the armour, maybe.
I can't say yes while you're clenching that spiked fist.

good: A tale about {subject}, told by someone who clearly lived through worse. Riveting.
You told that like a war story. I was holding my breath.
I'd never dare interrupt you, but I didn't want to anyway.
The bit where you slammed the table made me jump. Brilliant.
Gruesome, gripping and loud. Like you, and your armour.
bad: Every story with you ends in a body count, doesn't it?
Too much blood for a story about {subject}.
I nodded throughout because I was scared not to.
You told it like you were interrogating me.
Lovely. Can I leave now? Without you following?

good: A poem about {subject} from under that helmet. I'm genuinely moved.
Who knew a walking armoury had verse in it?
Your voice shook the windows, but the words were tender.
That was beautiful. I'll never tell anyone you can rhyme, promise.
Like a lullaby sung by a war drum.
bad: That poem sounded like a list of enemies.
Did it have to rhyme 'heart' with 'tear apart'?
It's hard to enjoy verse while you grip that mace.
Every stanza about {subject} felt like a threat.
I clapped. I'm not sure I had a choice.

landGood: Ha! The scary one is funny! Nobody warned me!
I laughed so hard I forgot about the skulls.
Okay, that got me. Your helmet rattling along was the best part.
Brilliant. And I'm laughing because I want to, not because of the axe.
Ha! Tell it again, the whole square should hear the walking fortress crack a joke.
landGroan: Ugh. Terrible. I'm laughing anyway, please note that I'm laughing.
That was awful, and I'll still pretend it was great. For safety.
Groan. Do they teach puns at warlord school?
Oh no. A pun. From under the horns.
Bad, but you said it so menacingly I chuckled.
flop: ...Was I supposed to laugh? Sorry, I'll laugh. Ha. Ha.
Silence. And now nervous silence, with clanking.
I didn't get it, and I'm too frightened to ask.
The crowd's very quiet. Probably the spikes.
That joke died faster than whoever owned those skulls.

good: Hm. Praise. Most people just back away from the spikes.
Good. Say it again, slower, so the skulls on my belt can hear.
The plate weighs forty kilos. Nice that somebody noticed the man inside.
I'll remember you said that. I remember everything. Ask my enemies.
That... was decent of you. Don't make me soft in front of the axe.
bad: Praise is what people say right before they ask me not to hit them.
Save it. Flattery bounces off steel.
You're sweating. Nobody sweats when they mean it.
I've had warlords praise me. They're all on this belt now.
Mm. And what do you want broken?

good: You like the spikes? Hand-filed. Every one of them.
Hah. Most say 'nice armour' with their eyes on the exit.
The helm was my grandfather's. So was the skull on it, in a way.
Kind words. I'll polish the pauldrons tonight in your honour.
Fine. You can stay within arm's reach. For now.
bad: Careful. People who admire the blade usually want to borrow it.
Compliment my maul again and it'll compliment you back.
That's not a compliment, that's a nervous habit.
You looked at the skulls first. Everyone looks at the skulls first.
Words. Iron doesn't care about words.

good: Hah. Nobody's told me to keep going since the last siege.
Right. I'll keep going. Something in my way will regret it.
Good. I needed a reason to put the gauntlets back on.
You've got nerve, cheering on a man dressed like a funeral.
Fine. Then I won't stop. I never really do.
bad: I don't need a cheering section. I need room to swing.
Encouragement. Cute. I was already going to win.
Pep talks are for people who lose. Look at me.
Don't pat the armour. It has edges for a reason.
Keep your hope. I run on spite and whetstone oil.

good: Terrifying, you say? Good. Took me years.
Go on. Tell me again how the room goes quiet when I walk in.
Hm. Even the visor's smiling a little.
Flattery from someone who isn't trembling. Rare. I'll allow it.
Yes, the horns are real. Yes, I sharpen them myself.
bad: Flatter me once more and I'll start wondering what you stole.
Too sweet. Sugar rusts plate.
I can hear your knees knocking under all that honey.
Liars talk fast around me. You're talking very fast.
Last man who buttered me up ended up as a doorstop.

good: Don't mention it. Really. I have a reputation.
You're welcome. Tell no one I was nice.
Hm. Gratitude. I'll hang it next to the skulls.
Glad to help. Usually I help things fall over.
Fine. You owe me nothing. Except silence about it.
bad: Thanks don't sharpen axes.
Keep it. I didn't do it for you, I did it because it was in the way.
Thank me again and I'll start charging.
Gratitude makes people soft. Stay hard, stay alive.
Don't thank me. Fear me. It lasts longer.

good: Small talk. Huh. Fine. Bought a new whetstone. Life's good.
Mostly I've been reforging the spikes. Bologna damp gets into everything.
Day was quiet. Nobody tried to rob me. Nobody ever tries twice.
Talk all you like. People rarely stand this close to me.
Not bad. Broke a door. Paid for it, even.
bad: I don't chat. I loom.
Weather, prices, trams. Get to the part where somebody bleeds.
You talk a lot for someone standing next to a war hammer.
Small talk is for small people.
Mm. Are you done? The maul's getting heavy.

good: Oh, I heard. And I know where he sleeps.
Interesting. I'll pay him a visit. In the full plate.
Ha. Rumours travel fast. I travel faster when I'm angry.
Keep talking. Names, streets, hours.
That's why the guild steps around me. Good to know it works.
bad: Gossip is for cowards. If you have a problem, I have an axe.
Don't whisper near me. Whispering makes me twitchy.
I don't care who's sleeping with who. I care who owes me.
Rumours about me? Let them run. They're all true.
Say it to their face. Or bring me, and I'll say it for you.

good: Rain's good. Washes the blood off the cobbles.
Cold, yes. Plate freezes to the skin. You get used to it.
Thunder suits me. Everyone thinks it's me walking.
Nice day for a siege. Or a stroll. Same thing.
Fog's coming in. Good. They won't see me until I'm there.
bad: Weather doesn't touch me. I'm wearing half a forge.
I don't feel the sun. Only the weight.
The sky can do what it likes. I'll still be here.
You're talking about clouds to a man with skulls on his shoulders.
Storms fear me. Didn't you know?

good: ...You've got guts. I might want to see them.
That one went between the plates. Well aimed.
Hm. Nobody's dared say that to me in years.
The visor's down so you can't see. But that stung.
Bold. Stupid, but bold. I'll let you walk away.
bad: Say that again. Slowly. While I put the gauntlet on.
Insults bounce. Steel doesn't.
I've been called worse by men with bigger weapons. They're quiet now.
Cute. Now count your teeth while you still have all of them.
Ha. Is that all? I eat insults for breakfast with the gravel.

good: Laugh at the horns, will you. ...Fine. They are a bit much.
Hah. All right. The cape is too long. I trip on it.
Mock the armour all you like. Just don't touch it.
You're the first to laugh in a year. The last one wasn't so lucky.
Grr. That one hit. I'll go clank somewhere else.
bad: Keep laughing. The skulls on my belt laughed too, once.
Funny. I'm smiling under the helm. You should worry.
Mockery from a man in a cardigan. Bold.
Go on, giggle. I can wait. I'm very patient for a monster.
Laugh while your ribs are still in one piece.

good: Hm. Too many spikes? ...Maybe I did snag the tram seat.
Fair. I don't have to break every door. Most open.
You're right. I'll try scaring people less. A bit less.
Not many tell me I'm wrong. Fewer survive it. Noted.
Fine. I'll take the skull off the helm. For dinner.
bad: Criticise the plate when you've worn it up a mountain.
You want me smaller? Quieter? Make me.
Opinions. Everyone has one. I have a war axe.
Tell me how to fight once you've won one.
The last critic needs a cane now.

good: ...You actually mean it. Respect. I'll stand down.
Huh. A threat that isn't shaking. All right, you win this one.
Easy. Easy. We're both dangerous. No need to prove it.
Fine. I'll leave. Not because I'm scared. Because you might be crazy.
Heh. You've got the look. We'll settle it another day.
bad: You're threatening the man with skulls on his belt. Think about that.
Go on then. Swing. I'll wait.
I've been threatened by a dragon. It's a rug now.
Cute. Do it again, I didn't hear the knees knocking over the words.
Threats are just promises you can't keep.

good: Hm. Most people flirt with me from across the street.
Careful. I'm all edges. ...But keep going.
You've got the nerve to wink at a man in spiked plate. I like nerve.
Under the helm I'm blushing. Tell anyone and you're dead.
Trouble, you are. Good. I collect trouble.
bad: Flirt with the axe. It's warmer than me.
No. I'm busy being terrifying.
Back up. The spikes on the elbows aren't decorative.
That's how my last squire got the scar.
I don't do sweet. I do siege.

good: Admire away. It took a smith three months to make me look like this.
You're staring at the plate. I'm glad. I polished it for nobody.
Nobody looks at me long. You do. Hm.
Yes, it's heavy. Yes, I can still carry you.
Go on. Look at the scars too. Each one's a story somebody else lost.
bad: Staring at a predator is how prey gets eaten.
Eyes up. Higher. Higher. That's the visor. Now go.
Admiration's cheap. Fear costs more.
Look all you want. You'll never get close enough to touch.
You're looking at me like a statue. Statues don't bite.

good: A letter. For me. I'll keep it inside the breastplate.
Hm. Nobody writes to me except to surrender.
Your handwriting shakes. Fear or feelings? ...Both is fine.
I'll read it alone. In the armoury. By the whetstone.
Kept it. Don't make a thing of it.
bad: I don't read letters. I read terrain.
Ink. On paper. To me. I'll use it to light the forge.
The last love letter I got was a ransom note.
Gauntlets tear paper. Sorry. Not sorry.
Write to someone who doesn't sleep in chainmail.

good: Singing. To me. Nobody sings to me, they sing about me, at funerals.
Not bad. Louder than my armour, even.
Hm. I'll bang the shield in time. That's applause, in my trade.
Keep singing. The skulls on my belt seem to like it.
That was... fine. Fine. Stop looking at me.
bad: Stop. Wolves sing better and I've killed those too.
My war horn has more tune than that.
Sing again and I'll show you a war cry.
Serenade the battlefield. It's used to screaming.
Enough. My ears are the only soft part left.

good: Dance. In fifty kilos of steel. ...One song.
I'll lead. Mind the spikes on the knees.
Hah. Fine. The floor might not survive it.
Nobody's asked since the war. Hold on tight.
Watch your feet. These boots have crushed armour.
bad: I don't dance. I march.
Dancing with me means bruises. Pass.
The only dance I know ends with someone on the floor.
No. The plate squeaks. Everybody stares.
Ask the hammer. It's lighter on its feet.

good: Careful. The gauntlet has edges. ...Fine. Hold on.
This hand broke a gate once. It's being gentle for you.
Hm. Warm. Mine's usually holding a hilt.
Don't squeeze. I don't know how not to squeeze back.
All right. Nobody's touched me without a weapon in years.
bad: Hands off. The last hand that grabbed mine is in a jar.
Grab my gauntlet again and you'll lose fingers. Spikes, I mean.
This hand is for axes.
No. My grip breaks things I'm fond of.
Let go. Slowly. Good.

good: Out. With me. People will cross the street. ...Yes.
Pick a place with high ceilings. The horns.
Fine. Somewhere with meat. Lots of meat.
Hah. I'll even leave the big axe at home. The small one comes.
A date. The waiter's going to drop everything. I'm in.
bad: Out where? Every bar in town has banned me.
No. I only go out to collect debts.
Restaurants empty when I walk in. Not much of an evening.
Ask someone who doesn't make children cry.
My evenings are for sharpening. Don't take it personally.

good: ...You'd say that to my face. To THIS face. All right. Me too.
Hm. The armour's thick. You got through it anyway.
Say it again. I've never heard it without a blade to my throat.
I don't do feelings. ...But I'd break a city for you.
Fine. You're mine now. Nobody touches what's mine.
bad: Feelings get people killed. Usually by me.
No. My heart is armoured too.
You love the helm, not what's under it. Trust me.
Walk away while I'm still being kind.
I'm a weapon. You don't fall in love with a weapon.

good: ...Helm off. Just this once.
Brave. Stupid and brave. Again.
You kissed a man in spiked plate. You're dangerous too.
Hm. Nobody gets that close and stays standing. Stay.
Don't tell the guild. They think I'm made of iron all the way through.
bad: Visor's down. You kissed steel. How was it?
No. Back up before the spikes decide for me.
Kiss me again and lose a lip on the gorget.
That's how the last one got a scar.
I bite. Not the fun way.

accept: {style}. Fine. Anyone who disagrees can talk to the axe.
Done. I'll guard it like a keep. {style} it is.
{style}. Hm. Rules are just walls. I'm good at walls.
Agreed. And anyone who breaks it answers to me.
Yes. Sworn on the skulls. That's binding where I'm from.
reject: {style}? I don't take terms. I set them.
No. I don't sign treaties I didn't write.
Rules for the heart. Ha. I'll keep mine in the plate.
Labels are for jars. I'm not a jar.
Pick a style for someone who surrenders.

good: {subject}. Good. Plenty of blood in that one.
Hm. Reminded me of a siege. In the good way.
Not bad. I'd have killed the villain sooner, though.
I listened all the way through without reaching for the axe. High praise.
Tell it again. Slower on the battle.
bad: Nobody died. What kind of story is that?
{subject}? I fell asleep in my armour. That's hard to do.
Too long. Get to the war.
The hero's soft. I'd have eaten him for breakfast.
Boring. I've lived worse and better.

good: A poem about {subject}. ...I'll carve it on the shield.
Hm. That one hit harder than a mace.
Again. The part about the dark.
I don't do poems. I'll make an exception. Once.
Good rhythm. Like a war drum.
bad: Rhymes. Pfah. Give me a war cry.
Poems don't stop an axe.
{subject}? Soft as wet bread.
That poem needs more skulls.
Stop before I recite mine. It's mostly screaming.

landGood: HAH! The helm rattled. That's how you know it's funny.
Ha... that one got under the plate.
Heh. I'll tell that one at the next execution.
Ha! You're funny. Funny people live longer near me.
Hah. Good. The skulls laughed too.
landGroan: Ugh. I've hit people for less. I'll let it go.
That was terrible. The axe is disappointed in you.
Groan. That was a groan. Under the visor. Be proud.
Bad. So bad. ...Tell me another.
Hnn. That's the kind of joke that gets you thrown off a wall. Fondly.
flop: ...The axe is getting bored.
Silence. You hear that? That's the skulls not laughing.
Was that the joke? Try again. Carefully.
Mm. My last jester told jokes like that. Once.
Nothing. Not a twitch. Want to see a twitch?
